verses.1:1: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who entered Egypt with Jacob; each man and his household came:
verses.1:4: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.
verses.1:5: Now all the souls who came forth from the loins of Jacob were seventy in number, for Joseph was already in Egypt.
verses.1:6: Then Joseph died, along with all his brethren and all that generation.
verses.1:7: But the sons of Israel were fruitful and teemed abundantly, and they multiplied and grew exceedingly mighty, so that the land was filled with them.
verses.1:8: Then a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.
verses.1:9: And he said to his people, "Behold, the people of the sons of Israel are more numerous and mightier than we.
verses.1:10: Come, let us deal shrewdly with them, lest they multiply, and it come to pass that when war breaks out, they also join themselves to those who hate us and fight against us, and go up out of the land."
verses.1:11: So they appointed taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens; and they built store cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses.
verses.1:12: Yet the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and spread abroad, so that the Egyptians came to dread the sons of Israel.
verses.1:13: And the Egyptians compelled the sons of Israel to serve with rigor.
verses.1:14: And they made their lives bitter with harsh bondage, in mortar and in brick, and in all manner of labor in the field; with rigor they imposed all their service upon them.
verses.1:15: Then the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, the name of one being Shiphrah and the name of the second Puah,
verses.1:16: and he said, "When you attend the Hebrew women in childbirth and look upon the birthstool, if it is a son, then you shall put him to death; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live."
verses.1:17: But the midwives feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had spoken to them, but kept the male children alive.
verses.1:18: So the king of Egypt summoned the midwives and said to them, "Why have you done this thing, and kept the male children alive?"
verses.1:19: And the midwives answered Pharaoh, "Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous, and they give birth before the midwife comes to them."
verses.1:20: Therefore God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied and grew exceedingly mighty.
verses.1:21: And it came to pass, because the midwives feared God, that He established households for them.
verses.1:22: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, "Every son who is born you shall cast into the Nile, and every daughter you shall keep alive."
verses.2:1: Now a man of the house of Levi went and took as his wife a daughter of Levi.
verses.2:2: And the woman conceived and bore a son; and when she saw that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.
verses.2:3: But when she could no longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes and coated it with bitumen and pitch; then she placed the child in it and set it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile.
verses.2:4: And his sister stationed herself at a distance, to learn what would be done to him.
verses.2:5: Then the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the Nile, while her maidens walked beside the Nile; and she saw the ark in the midst of the reeds, and she sent her maidservant to take it.
verses.2:6: And when she opened it, she saw the child, and behold, the boy was weeping. So she took pity on him and said, "This is one of the children of the Hebrews."
verses.2:7: Then his sister said to the daughter of Pharaoh, "Shall I go and call a nursing woman for you from among the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?"
verses.2:8: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, "Go." So the maiden went and called the child's mother.
verses.2:9: And the daughter of Pharaoh said to her, "Take this child away and nurse him for me, and I myself will give you your wages." So the woman took the child and nursed him.
verses.2:10: And the child grew, and she brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, saying, "Because I drew him out of the water."
verses.2:11: Now it came to pass in those days, when Moses had grown up, that he went out to his brethren and looked upon their burdens; and he saw an Egyptian man striking a Hebrew man, one of his brethren.
verses.2:12: So he turned this way and that, and when he saw that there was no one, he struck down the Egyptian and hid him in the sand.
verses.2:13: And he went out on the second day, and behold, two Hebrew men were quarreling together; and he said to the one who was in the wrong, "Why do you strike your companion?"
verses.2:14: And he answered, "Who appointed you a prince and a judge over us? Do you intend to slay me as you slew the Egyptian?" Then Moses was afraid and said, "Surely this matter has become known!"
verses.2:15: When Pharaoh heard of this matter, he sought to slay Moses; but Moses fled from the presence of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well.
verses.2:16: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters; and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.
verses.2:17: Then the shepherds came and drove them away; but Moses rose up and rescued them, and watered their flock.
verses.2:18: When they came to Reuel their father, he said, "Why have you returned so soon today?"
verses.2:19: And they answered, "An Egyptian man delivered us from the hand of the shepherds; moreover, he even drew water for us and watered the flock."
verses.2:20: So he said to his daughters, "And where is he? Why is it that you have left the man behind? Call him, that he may eat bread."
verses.2:21: And Moses consented to dwell with the man, and he gave Zipporah his daughter to Moses.
verses.2:22: And she bore a son, and he called his name Gershom; for he said, "I have been a sojourner in a foreign land."
verses.2:23: Now it came to pass during those many days that the king of Egypt died; and the sons of Israel groaned because of the bondage and cried out, and their cry for help ascended to God because of the bondage.
verses.2:24: So God heard their groaning, and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
verses.2:25: And God beheld the sons of Israel, and God knew.
verses.3:1: Now Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian; and he led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God.
verses.3:2: Then the Angel of the LORD appeared to him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush; and as he looked, behold, the bush burned with fire, yet the bush was not being consumed.
verses.3:3: And Moses said, "Let me turn aside now and behold this great sight, why the bush does not burn up."
verses.3:4: When the LORD saw that he had turned aside to look, God called to him out of the midst of the bush and said, "Moses, Moses!" And he answered, "Here I am."
verses.3:5: Then He said, "Do not come near here; remove your sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground."
verses.3:6: And He said, "I am the God of your father—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob." Then Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to gaze upon God.
verses.3:7: And the LORD said, "I have surely beheld the affliction of My people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their outcry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.
verses.3:8: Therefore I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up from that land to a good and spacious land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites.
verses.3:9: And now, behold, the outcry of the sons of Israel has come to Me, and I have also seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.
verses.3:10: Now therefore, come, and I will send you to Pharaoh, that you may bring My people, the sons of Israel, out of Egypt."
verses.3:11: But Moses said to God, "Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt?"
verses.3:12: And He said, "Assuredly I will be with you; and this shall be the sign to you that I Myself have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God upon this mountain."
verses.3:13: Then Moses said to God, "Behold, when I come to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'The God of your fathers has sent me to you,' and they say to me, 'What is His name?'—what shall I answer them?"
verses.3:14: Then God answered Moses, "I AM WHO I AM." And He said, "This you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'I AM has sent me to you.'"
verses.3:15: Moreover God said to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the sons of Israel: 'The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.' This is My name forever, and this is My memorial from generation to generation.
verses.3:16: Go and gather the elders of Israel together, and say to them, 'The LORD, the God of your fathers—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—has appeared to me, saying, "I have surely visited you and observed what has been done to you in Egypt,
verses.3:17: and I have said that I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt to the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, to a land flowing with milk and honey."'
verses.3:18: Then they will heed your voice; and you shall go, you and the elders of Israel, to the king of Egypt, and you shall say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us; and now, please, let us go a journey of three days into the wilderness, that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.'
verses.3:19: Yet I Myself know that the king of Egypt will not permit you to go, not even by a mighty hand.
verses.3:20: So I will stretch forth My hand and strike Egypt with all My wonders which I will perform in its midst; and after that he will send you away.
verses.3:21: And I will grant this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians; and it shall come to pass, when you go, that you shall not go empty-handed.
verses.3:22: Rather, every woman shall ask of her neighbor, and of her who sojourns in her house, articles of silver, articles of gold, and garments; and you shall put them upon your sons and upon your daughters. Thus you shall plunder the Egyptians."
verses.4:1: Then Moses answered and said, "But behold, they will not believe me, nor will they listen to my voice; for they will say, 'The LORD has not appeared to you.'"
verses.4:2: So the LORD said to him, "What is this in your hand?" And he said, "A staff."
verses.4:3: And He said, "Cast it to the ground." So he cast it to the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.
verses.4:4: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand and take hold of its tail"—and he stretched out his hand and grasped it, and it became a staff in his palm—
verses.4:5: "so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you."
verses.4:6: And the LORD spoke to him again, "Put your hand now into your bosom." So he put his hand into his bosom; and he brought it out, and behold, his hand was leprous, like snow.
verses.4:7: Then He said, "Put your hand back into your bosom." So he put his hand back into his bosom, and brought it out from his bosom, and behold, it was restored like his own flesh.
verses.4:8: "And it shall be, if they do not believe you nor heed the voice of the first sign, that they will believe the voice of the latter sign.
verses.4:9: And it shall be, if they do not believe even these two signs nor listen to your voice, that you shall take some of the water of the Nile and pour it on the dry ground; and the water that you take from the Nile shall become blood on the dry ground."
verses.4:10: Then Moses said to the LORD, "O Lord, I am not a man of words, neither in time past nor since You have spoken to Your servant; for I am heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue."
verses.4:11: And the LORD said to him, "Who has made the mouth of man? Or who makes the mute, or the deaf, or the seeing, or the blind? Is it not I, the LORD?
verses.4:12: Now therefore, go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you shall speak."
verses.4:13: But he said, "O Lord, please send by the hand of whomever You will send."
verses.4:14: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, "Is there not Aaron your brother, the Levite? I know that he can indeed speak well. And behold, he is also coming out to meet you; and when he sees you, he will rejoice in his heart.
verses.4:15: You shall speak to him and put the words in his mouth; and I will be with your mouth and with his mouth, and I will teach you what you shall do.
verses.4:16: And he shall speak for you to the people; and it shall be that he himself shall be a mouth for you, and you shall be to him as God.
verses.4:17: And you shall take this staff in your hand, with which you shall perform the signs."
verses.4:18: So Moses went and returned to Jether his father-in-law, and said to him, "Please let me go and return to my brethren who are in Egypt, and see whether they are still alive." And Jethro said to Moses, "Go in peace."
verses.4:19: Now the LORD said to Moses in Midian, "Go, return to Egypt; for all the men who were seeking your life are dead."
verses.4:20: So Moses took his wife and his sons and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Egypt. And Moses took the staff of God in his hand.
verses.4:21: And the LORD said to Moses, "When you go back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in your hand; yet I will harden his heart, so that he will not let the people go.
verses.4:22: Then you shall say to Pharaoh, 'Thus says the LORD: Israel is My son, My firstborn.
verses.4:23: And I have said to you, "Let My son go that he may serve Me," yet you have refused to let him go; behold, I will slay your son, your firstborn.'"
verses.4:24: Now it came to pass on the way, at the lodging place, that the LORD met him and sought to put him to death.
verses.4:25: Then Zipporah took a flint and cut off the foreskin of her son, and touched it to his feet, and said, "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me!"
verses.4:26: So He let him alone. Then she said, "A bridegroom of blood, because of the circumcision."
verses.4:27: And the LORD said to Aaron, "Go into the wilderness to meet Moses." So he went and met him at the mountain of God, and kissed him.
verses.4:28: Then Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD with which He had sent him, and all the signs which He had commanded him.
verses.4:29: So Moses and Aaron went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Israel.
verses.4:30: And Aaron spoke all the words which the LORD had spoken to Moses, and he performed the signs in the sight of the people.
verses.4:31: So the people believed; and when they heard that the LORD had visited the children of Israel and that He had looked upon their affliction, they bowed their heads and worshiped.
verses.5:1: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in and said to Pharaoh, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Let My people go, that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.'"
verses.5:2: And Pharaoh said, "Who is the LORD, that I should heed His voice to let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, nor will I let Israel go."
verses.5:3: So they said, "The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please let us go a three days' journey into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God, lest He fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword."
verses.5:4: Then the king of Egypt said to them, "Moses and Aaron, why do you draw the people away from their labor? Go back to your burdens!"
verses.5:5: And Pharaoh said, "Behold, the people of the land are now many, and you make them rest from their burdens!"
verses.5:6: So on that same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their officers, saying,
verses.5:7: "You shall no longer give the people straw to make bricks as before; let them go and gather straw for themselves.
verses.5:8: Yet the quota of bricks which they made previously you shall lay upon them; you shall not reduce it at all. For they are idle; therefore they cry out, saying, 'Let us go and sacrifice to our God.'
verses.5:9: Let the labor be made heavier upon the men, that they may toil at it, and let them not pay regard to lying words."
verses.5:10: So the taskmasters of the people and their officers went out and spoke to the people, saying, "Thus says Pharaoh: 'I will not give you straw.
verses.5:11: Go yourselves, get straw for yourselves wherever you can find it; for nothing at all shall be reduced from your labor.'"
verses.5:12: So the people scattered throughout all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.
verses.5:13: And the taskmasters pressed them, saying, "Complete your work, your daily portion, just as when there was straw."
verses.5:14: And the officers of the children of Israel, whom Pharaoh's taskmasters had set over them, were beaten and asked, "Why have you not completed your allotted task in making bricks as before, both yesterday and today?"
verses.5:15: Then the officers of the children of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, "Why do you deal thus with your servants?
verses.5:16: No straw is given to your servants, yet they say to us, 'Make bricks!' And behold, your servants are beaten, though the fault is with your own people."
verses.5:17: But he said, "You are idle, idle! Therefore you say, 'Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.'
verses.5:18: Go now and work; for no straw shall be given to you, yet you shall deliver the full tally of bricks."
verses.5:19: And the officers of the children of Israel saw that they were in distress when it was said, "You shall not reduce anything from your bricks, your daily portion."
verses.5:20: Then they came upon Moses and Aaron standing to meet them as they came out from Pharaoh.
verses.5:21: And they said to them, "May the LORD look upon you and judge, because you have made our odor foul in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to slay us."
verses.5:22: So Moses returned to the LORD and said, "O Lord, why have You brought harm upon this people? Why is it that You have sent me?
verses.5:23: For ever since I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has done harm to this people; and You have not delivered Your people at all."
verses.6:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh; for with a strong hand he will let them go, and with a strong hand he will drive them out of his land."
verses.6:2: And God spoke to Moses and said to him, "I am the LORD.
verses.6:3: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob as God Almighty, yet by My name the LORD I did not make Myself known to them.
verses.6:4: And I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings, in which they sojourned.
verses.6:5: And I have also heard the groaning of the children of Israel, whom the Egyptians hold in bondage, and I have remembered My covenant.
verses.6:6: Therefore say to the children of Israel: 'I am the LORD; I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians, I will rescue you from their bondage, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments.
verses.6:7: And I will take you to Myself as a people, and I will be your God; then you shall know that I am the LORD your God, who brings you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians.
verses.6:8: And I will bring you into the land that I lifted up My hand to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it to you as a possession. I am the LORD.'"
verses.6:9: So Moses spoke thus to the children of Israel; yet they did not listen to Moses, because of brokenness of spirit and harsh bondage.
verses.6:10: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.6:11: "Go in, speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land."
verses.6:12: And Moses spoke before the LORD, saying, "Behold, the children of Israel have not listened to me; how then shall Pharaoh listen to me, since I am of uncircumcised lips?"
verses.6:13: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, and gave them a charge to the children of Israel and to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
verses.6:14: These are the heads of their fathers' houses: The sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi; these are the families of Reuben.
verses.6:15: And the sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman; these are the families of Simeon.
verses.6:16: And these are the names of the sons of Levi according to their generations: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. And the years of the life of Levi were one hundred and thirty-seven years.
verses.6:17: The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei, according to their families.
verses.6:18: And the sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. And the years of the life of Kohath were one hundred and thirty-three years.
verses.6:19: And the sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites according to their generations.
verses.6:20: Now Amram took for himself Jochebed, his father's sister, as wife, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. And the years of the life of Amram were one hundred and thirty-seven years.
verses.6:21: And the sons of Izhar were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
verses.6:22: And the sons of Uzziel were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
verses.6:23: And Aaron took for himself Elisheba, the daughter of Amminadab, the sister of Nahshon, as wife; and she bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
verses.6:24: And the sons of Korah were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph; these are the families of the Korahites.
verses.6:25: And Eleazar, Aaron's son, took for himself one of the daughters of Putiel as wife, and she bore him Phinehas. These are the heads of the fathers' houses of the Levites according to their families.
verses.6:26: These are the same Aaron and Moses to whom the LORD said, "Bring out the children of Israel from the land of Egypt according to their hosts."
verses.6:27: These are the ones who spoke to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to bring out the children of Israel from Egypt. These are that same Moses and Aaron.
verses.6:28: And it came to pass, on the day when the LORD spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
verses.6:29: that the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "I am the LORD. Speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt all that I speak to you."
verses.6:30: And Moses said before the LORD, "Behold, I am of uncircumcised lips; how then shall Pharaoh listen to me?"
verses.7:1: And the LORD said to Moses, "See, I have made you as God to Pharaoh, and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.
verses.7:2: You shall speak all that I command you, and Aaron your brother shall speak to Pharaoh, that he let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.7:3: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.
verses.7:4: Yet Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that I may lay My hand upon Egypt and bring out My hosts, My people the children of Israel, from the land of Egypt by great judgments.
verses.7:5: And the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I stretch out My hand upon Egypt and bring out the children of Israel from among them."
verses.7:6: So Moses and Aaron did; just as the LORD commanded them, so they did.
verses.7:7: Now Moses was eighty years old and Aaron was eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh.
verses.7:8: And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,
verses.7:9: "When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, 'Show a wonder for yourselves,' then you shall say to Aaron, 'Take your rod and cast it before Pharaoh, and it shall become a serpent.'"
verses.7:10: So Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and they did so, just as the LORD had commanded. And Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.
verses.7:11: Then Pharaoh also summoned the wise men and the sorcerers; and they also, the magicians of Egypt, did in like manner with their enchantments.
verses.7:12: For each man cast down his rod, and they became serpents; yet Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.
verses.7:13: And Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.7:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh's heart is stubborn; he refuses to let the people go.
verses.7:15: Go to Pharaoh in the morning—behold, he is going out to the water—and you shall stand by the bank of the Nile to meet him; and the rod that was turned into a serpent you shall take in your hand.
verses.7:16: And you shall say to him, 'The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has sent me to you, saying, "Let My people go, that they may serve Me in the wilderness," yet behold, until now you have not listened.
verses.7:17: Thus says the LORD: "By this you shall know that I am the LORD. Behold, I will strike the waters that are in the Nile with the rod that is in My hand, and they shall be turned to blood.
verses.7:18: And the fish that are in the Nile shall die, and the Nile shall become foul, and the Egyptians will loathe to drink water from the Nile."'"
verses.7:19: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Take your rod and stretch out your hand over the waters of Egypt, over their rivers, over their canals, over their ponds, and over all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and there shall be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in wood and in stone.'"
verses.7:20: And Moses and Aaron did so, just as the LORD commanded. He lifted up the rod and struck the waters that were in the Nile, in the sight of Pharaoh and in the sight of his servants; and all the waters that were in the Nile were turned to blood.
verses.7:21: And the fish that were in the Nile died, and the Nile became foul, so that the Egyptians could not drink water from the Nile; and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.7:22: Then the magicians of Egypt did so with their secret arts; and Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.7:23: And Pharaoh turned and went into his house, and he did not take even this to heart.
verses.7:24: So all the Egyptians dug all around the Nile for water to drink, because they could not drink of the water of the Nile.
verses.7:25: And seven full days passed after the LORD had struck the Nile.
verses.7:26: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and say to him, 'Thus says the LORD: "Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
verses.7:27: But if you refuse to let them go, behold, I will smite all your territory with frogs.
verses.7:28: So the Nile shall swarm with frogs, which shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber, and upon your bed, and into the house of your servants, and upon your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneading bowls.
verses.7:29: And the frogs shall come up upon you, and upon your people, and upon all your servants."'"
verses.8:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your hand with your rod over the streams, over the rivers, and over the pools, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:2: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters of Egypt, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
verses.8:3: And the magicians did likewise with their secret arts, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.
verses.8:4: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and Aaron and said, "Plead with the LORD, that He may take away the frogs from me and from my people; and I will send away the people, that they may sacrifice to the LORD."
verses.8:5: And Moses said to Pharaoh, "Accept the honor of telling me: for what time shall I plead for you, for your servants, and for your people, to cut off the frogs from you and from your houses, that they may remain only in the River?"
verses.8:6: And he said, "For tomorrow." And he said, "Let it be according to your word, that you may know that there is none like the LORD our God.
verses.8:7: And the frogs shall depart from you, from your houses, from your servants, and from your people; they shall remain only in the River."
verses.8:8: Then Moses and Aaron went out from Pharaoh, and Moses cried out to the LORD concerning the frogs which He had set upon Pharaoh.
verses.8:9: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses. So the frogs died out of the houses, out of the courtyards, and out of the fields.
verses.8:10: And they gathered them together in heaps upon heaps, and the land stank.
verses.8:11: But when Pharaoh saw that there was relief, he hardened his heart and did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.8:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Say to Aaron, 'Stretch out your rod and strike the dust of the land, that it may become gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.'"
verses.8:13: And they did so. For Aaron stretched out his hand with his rod and struck the dust of the earth, and there were gnats on man and on beast. All the dust of the land became gnats throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.8:14: Now the magicians tried likewise with their secret arts to bring forth gnats, but they could not. So the gnats were on man and on beast.
verses.8:15: Then the magicians said to Pharaoh, "This is the finger of God." Yet Pharaoh's heart grew hard, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken.
verses.8:16: And the LORD said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh—behold, he is going out to the water—and say to him, 'Thus says the LORD: Send away My people, that they may serve Me.
verses.8:17: For if you will not send away My people, behold, I am sending swarms of flies upon you, upon your servants, upon your people, and into your houses; and the houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with the swarms of flies, and also the ground on which they stand.
verses.8:18: And in that day I will set apart the land of Goshen, in which My people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there, in order that you may know that I am the LORD in the midst of the land.
verses.8:19: And I will set a distinction between My people and your people. Tomorrow this sign shall come to pass.'"
verses.8:20: And the LORD did so. A heavy swarm of flies came into the house of Pharaoh and into the houses of his servants; and throughout all the land of Egypt, the land was ruined because of the swarms of flies.
verses.8:21: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, "Go, sacrifice to your God within the land."
verses.8:22: And Moses said, "It is not right to do so, for we would be sacrificing what is an abomination to the Egyptians to the LORD our God. Behold, if we sacrifice what is an abomination to the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us?
verses.8:23: We will go a journey of three days into the wilderness and sacrifice to the LORD our God, as He shall say to us."
verses.8:24: So Pharaoh said, "I will send you away, that you may sacrifice to the LORD your God in the wilderness; only you shall not go very far away. Plead for me."
verses.8:25: Then Moses said, "Behold, I am going out from you, and I will plead with the LORD that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow. Only let Pharaoh not deal deceitfully again by refusing to send the people away to sacrifice to the LORD."
verses.8:26: So Moses went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.
verses.8:27: And the LORD did according to the word of Moses, and removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; not one remained.
verses.8:28: Yet Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and did not send the people away.
verses.9:1: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh and speak to him, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Send away My people, that they may serve Me.
verses.9:2: For if you refuse to send them away, and still hold them fast,
verses.9:3: behold, the hand of the LORD shall be upon your livestock which are in the field, upon the horses, upon the donkeys, upon the camels, upon the herds, and upon the flocks—a very grievous pestilence.
verses.9:4: And the LORD shall make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that nothing shall die of all that belongs to the children of Israel.'"
verses.9:5: And the LORD appointed a set time, saying, "Tomorrow the LORD shall do this thing in the land."
verses.9:6: So the LORD did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of Egypt died; but of the livestock of the children of Israel, not one died.
verses.9:7: And Pharaoh sent, and behold, not even one of the livestock of Israel had died. Yet the heart of Pharaoh became hardened, and he did not send the people away.
verses.9:8: Then the LORD said to Moses and to Aaron, "Take for yourselves handfuls of soot from a kiln, and let Moses scatter it toward the heavens in the sight of Pharaoh.
verses.9:9: And it shall become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and it shall become boils breaking out with blisters on man and on beast throughout all the land of Egypt."
verses.9:10: So they took soot from the kiln and stood before Pharaoh, and Moses scattered it toward the heavens; and it became boils breaking out with blisters on man and on beast.
verses.9:11: And the magicians could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were upon the magicians and upon all the Egyptians.
verses.9:12: But the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses.
verses.9:13: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and say to him, 'Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: Send away My people, that they may serve Me.
verses.9:14: For at this time I am sending all My plagues against your heart, and upon your servants and upon your people, in order that you may know that there is none like Me in all the earth.
verses.9:15: For by now I could have stretched out My hand and struck you and your people with pestilence, and you would have been cut off from the earth.
verses.9:16: Indeed, for this very purpose I have caused you to stand: to show you My power, and that My name may be declared in all the earth.
verses.9:17: You still exalt yourself against My people, so as not to send them away.
verses.9:18: Behold, about this time tomorrow I will rain down a very heavy hail, such as has not been in Egypt from the day it was founded even until now.
verses.9:19: Now therefore send, bring your livestock and all that you have in the field to safety; every man and beast that is found in the field and is not gathered home—the hail shall come down upon them, and they shall die.'"
verses.9:20: Whoever feared the word of the LORD among the servants of Pharaoh made his servants and his livestock flee into the houses.
verses.9:21: But whoever did not set his heart to the word of the LORD left his servants and his livestock in the field.
verses.9:22: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward the heavens, that there may be hail throughout all the land of Egypt—upon man, upon beast, and upon every herb of the field in the land of Egypt."
verses.9:23: So Moses stretched out his rod toward the heavens; and the LORD sent thunder and hail, and fire ran down to the earth. And the LORD rained hail upon the land of Egypt.
verses.9:24: Thus there was hail, and fire flashing continually in the midst of the hail, exceedingly heavy, such as had never been in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.
verses.9:25: And the hail struck throughout all the land of Egypt all that was in the field, both man and beast; and the hail struck every herb of the field and shattered every tree of the field.
verses.9:26: Only in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel were, there was no hail.
verses.9:27: Then Pharaoh sent and summoned Moses and Aaron, and said to them, "I have sinned this time. The LORD is righteous, and I and my people are wicked.
verses.9:28: Plead with the LORD, for there has been enough of the thunderings of God and hail; and I will send you away, and you shall stay no longer."
verses.9:29: And Moses said to him, "As soon as I have gone out of the city, I will spread out my hands to the LORD; the thunder shall cease, and there shall be hail no more, in order that you may know that the earth belongs to the LORD.
verses.9:30: But as for you and your servants, I know that you do not yet fear the LORD God."
verses.9:31: Now the flax and the barley were struck down, for the barley was in the ear and the flax was in bud.
verses.9:32: But the wheat and the spelt were not struck down, for they ripen late.
verses.9:33: So Moses went out of the city from Pharaoh and spread out his hands to the LORD; and the thunder and the hail ceased, and the rain no longer poured down upon the earth.
verses.9:34: And when Pharaoh saw that the rain, the hail, and the thunder had ceased, he sinned yet again; and he hardened his heart, both he and his servants.
verses.9:35: So the heart of Pharaoh grew hard, and he did not send away the children of Israel, just as the LORD had spoken by the hand of Moses.
verses.10:1: And the LORD said to Moses, "Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that I may place these signs of Mine in his midst,
verses.10:2: and that you may recount in the ears of your son and your son's son how I have dealt severely with Egypt, and My signs which I have set among them; and you shall know that I am the LORD."
verses.10:3: And Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and said to him, "Thus says the LORD, the God of the Hebrews: 'How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, that they may serve Me.
verses.10:4: For if you refuse to let My people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your borders.
verses.10:5: And they shall cover the surface of the land, so that no one shall be able to see the land; and they shall devour the remnant of what escaped, which remains to you from the hail, and they shall devour every tree that sprouts for you out of the field.
verses.10:6: And your houses shall be filled, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians, such as neither your fathers nor your fathers' fathers have seen, from the day that they were upon the earth until this day.'" And he turned and went out from Pharaoh.
verses.10:7: Then Pharaoh's servants said to him, "How long shall this man be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may serve the LORD their God. Do you not yet know that Egypt is ruined?"
verses.10:8: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, "Go, serve the LORD your God. Who, specifically, are the ones going?"
verses.10:9: And Moses said, "With our young and with our old we will go; with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds we will go, for we have a feast to the LORD."
verses.10:10: And he said to them, "May the LORD indeed be with you, just as I let you and your little ones go! Beware, for evil is before your faces.
verses.10:11: Not so! Go now, you who are men, and serve the LORD, for that is what you are seeking." And they were driven out from the presence of Pharaoh.
verses.10:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up over the land of Egypt and devour every herb of the land, all that the hail has left."
verses.10:13: So Moses stretched out his rod over the land of Egypt, and the LORD drove an east wind across the land all that day and all that night. When morning came, the east wind had brought the locusts.
verses.10:14: And the locusts went up over all the land of Egypt and settled within all the territory of Egypt, exceedingly grievous; before them there had never been such locusts as these, nor after them shall there ever be such again.
verses.10:15: And they covered the surface of the whole land, so that the land was darkened; and they devoured every herb of the land and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left. Thus nothing green remained on the trees or among the herbs of the field throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.10:16: Then Pharaoh made haste to call for Moses and Aaron, and said, "I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
verses.10:17: Now therefore, please forgive my sin only this once, and plead with the LORD your God that He may remove from me only this death."
verses.10:18: So he went out from Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.
verses.10:19: And the LORD turned an exceedingly strong west wind, which lifted up the locusts and drove them into the Red Sea; not one locust remained within all the borders of Egypt.
verses.10:20: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go.
verses.10:21: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand toward heaven, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness that may be felt."
verses.10:22: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and there was thick darkness throughout all the land of Egypt for three days.
verses.10:23: No one saw his brother, nor did anyone rise from his place for three days; yet all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.
verses.10:24: Then Pharaoh called to Moses and said, "Go, serve the LORD; only let your flocks and your herds be left behind. Your little ones also may go with you."
verses.10:25: But Moses said, "You yourself must also put into our hands sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may offer them to the LORD our God.
verses.10:26: Our livestock also shall go with us; not a hoof shall be left behind, for from them we must take to serve the LORD our God, and we ourselves do not know with what we must serve the LORD until we arrive there."
verses.10:27: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he was not willing to let them go.
verses.10:28: Then Pharaoh said to him, "Depart from me! Take heed to yourself that you do not see my face again, for in the day you see my face, you shall die."
verses.10:29: And Moses said, "You have spoken rightly; I shall never see your face again."
verses.11:1: And the LORD said to Moses, "Yet one more plague I will bring upon Pharaoh and upon Egypt. Afterward he will let you go from this place; when he lets you go altogether, he will surely drive you out from here.
verses.11:2: Speak now in the ears of the people, and let every man ask from his neighbor, and every woman from her neighbor, articles of silver and articles of gold."
verses.11:3: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was exceedingly great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh's servants and in the sight of the people.
verses.11:4: Then Moses said, "Thus says the LORD: 'About midnight I will go forth into the midst of Egypt,
verses.11:5: and every firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits upon his throne, even to the firstborn of the maidservant who is behind the handmill, and every firstborn of the beasts.
verses.11:6: And there shall be a great outcry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as has never been before, nor shall there ever be the like again.
verses.11:7: But against none of the children of Israel shall a dog move its tongue, from man even to beast, that you may know that the LORD makes a distinction between Egypt and Israel.'
verses.11:8: And all these your servants shall come down to me and bow down to me, saying, 'Depart, you and all the people who follow at your feet!' And after that I will go out." Then he went out from Pharaoh in burning anger.
verses.11:9: And the LORD said to Moses, "Pharaoh will not heed you, so that My wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt."
verses.11:10: So Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh; yet the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he did not let the children of Israel go out of his land.
verses.12:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.12:2: "This month shall be to you the beginning of months; it shall be to you the first among the months of the year.
verses.12:3: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, 'On the tenth day of this month, each man shall take for himself a lamb for a father's house, a lamb for each household.
verses.12:4: And if the household is too small for a lamb, then he and his neighbor nearest to his house shall take one according to the number of persons; according to what each man can eat, you shall reckon your count for the lamb.
verses.12:5: Your lamb shall be without blemish, a male of the first year; you may take it from the sheep or from the goats.
verses.12:6: And you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of this month; then the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it at twilight.
verses.12:7: And they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel of the houses in which they shall eat it.
verses.12:8: And they shall eat the flesh that night, roasted in fire; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it.
verses.12:9: Do not eat any of it raw, nor boiled at all in water, but roasted in fire—its head with its legs and its inward parts.
verses.12:10: And you shall leave none of it until morning; and what remains of it until morning you shall burn in the fire.
verses.12:11: And in this manner you shall eat it: with your loins girded, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste. It is the LORD's Passover.
verses.12:12: And I will pass through the land of Egypt on that night, and I will strike every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from man to beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments: I am the LORD.
verses.12:13: And the blood shall be a sign for you upon the houses where you are; and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.
verses.12:14: And this day shall be a memorial to you, and you shall observe it as a feast to the LORD; throughout your generations you shall observe it as a perpetual statute.
verses.12:15: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; surely on the first day you shall put away leaven from your houses. For whoever eats anything leavened from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
verses.12:16: On the first day there shall be a holy convocation, and on the seventh day there shall be a holy convocation for you. No manner of work shall be done on them; only that which every soul must eat, that alone may be prepared by you.
verses.12:17: And you shall observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I have brought your hosts out of the land of Egypt; therefore you shall keep this day throughout your generations as an everlasting statute.
verses.12:18: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month at evening.
verses.12:19: For seven days no leaven shall be found in your houses, for whoever eats anything leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether a sojourner or a native of the land.
verses.12:20: You shall eat nothing leavened; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.'"
verses.12:21: Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, "Draw out and take for yourselves lambs according to your families, and slaughter the Passover lamb.
verses.12:22: And you shall take a bunch of hyssop, dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and touch the lintel and the two doorposts with the blood that is in the basin. And none of you shall go out from the doorway of his house until morning.
verses.12:23: For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when He sees the blood upon the lintel and upon the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over the doorway and will not allow the destroyer to come into your houses to strike you.
verses.12:24: And you shall observe this thing as a statute for you and for your children forever.
verses.12:25: And it shall come to pass, when you enter the land which the LORD will give you, just as He has spoken, that you shall keep this service.
verses.12:26: And it shall come to pass, when your children say to you, 'What is this service to you?'
verses.12:27: that you shall say, 'It is the Passover sacrifice to the LORD, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians and delivered our households.'" Then the people bowed down and worshiped.
verses.12:28: And the children of Israel went and did it; just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
verses.12:29: And it came to pass at midnight that the LORD struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat upon his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and every firstborn of the livestock.
verses.12:30: Then Pharaoh arose in the night, he, all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great outcry in Egypt, for there was not a house in which there was not one dead.
verses.12:31: And he summoned Moses and Aaron by night and said, "Arise, go forth from among my people, both you and the children of Israel; and go, serve the LORD as you have spoken.
verses.12:32: Take also your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and go; and bless me also."
verses.12:33: And the Egyptians pressed urgently upon the people to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, "We are all dead!"
verses.12:34: So the people took up their dough before it was leavened, with their kneading bowls bound up in their cloaks upon their shoulders.
verses.12:35: Now the children of Israel had done according to the word of Moses, for they had asked of the Egyptians articles of silver, articles of gold, and garments.
verses.12:36: And the LORD had given the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they granted them what they asked; and thus they plundered the Egyptians.
verses.12:37: Then the children of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, besides little ones.
verses.12:38: A mixed multitude also went up with them, and flocks and herds, a very great abundance of livestock.
verses.12:39: And they baked unleavened cakes from the dough which they had brought out of Egypt, for it was not leavened, because they were driven out of Egypt and could not delay, nor had they prepared any provisions for themselves.
verses.12:40: Now the sojourning of the children of Israel who dwelt in Egypt was four hundred and thirty years.
verses.12:41: And it came to pass at the end of four hundred and thirty years—on that very day—all the hosts of the LORD went out from the land of Egypt.
verses.12:42: It is a night of solemn watchfulness to the LORD for bringing them out of the land of Egypt; this is that night of the LORD, to be solemnly kept by all the children of Israel throughout their generations.
verses.12:43: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "This is the ordinance of the Passover: No foreigner shall eat of it.
verses.12:44: But every man's servant who is bought with money, once you have circumcised him, then he may eat of it.
verses.12:45: A temporary resident and a hired servant shall not eat of it.
verses.12:46: It shall be eaten in one house; you shall not carry any of the flesh outside the house, nor shall you break a bone of it.
verses.12:47: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.
verses.12:48: And when a sojourner dwells with you and would keep the Passover to the LORD, let every male belonging to him be circumcised, and then let him draw near to keep it; and he shall be as a native of the land. But no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.
verses.12:49: One law shall be for the native-born and for the sojourner who dwells among you."
verses.12:50: Thus all the children of Israel did; just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.
verses.12:51: And it came to pass on that very day that the LORD brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their hosts.
verses.13:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.13:2: "Sanctify to Me every firstborn, whatever opens every womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast; it belongs to Me."
verses.13:3: And Moses said to the people, "Remember this day in which you came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the LORD brought you out from this place, and no leavened bread shall be eaten.
verses.13:4: On this day you are going out, in the month of Abib.
verses.13:5: And it shall come to pass, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, which He swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall perform this service in this month.
verses.13:6: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the LORD.
verses.13:7: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; no leavened bread shall be seen among you, nor shall leaven be seen among you within all your borders.
verses.13:8: And you shall declare to your son in that day, saying, 'This is done because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.'
verses.13:9: And it shall be a sign to you upon your hand and a memorial between your eyes, so that the law of the LORD may be in your mouth; for with a strong hand the LORD has brought you out of Egypt.
verses.13:10: Therefore you shall keep this statute at its appointed season from year to year.
verses.13:11: And it shall come to pass, when the LORD brings you into the land of the Canaanites, as He swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,
verses.13:12: that you shall set apart to the LORD every firstborn that opens the womb, and every firstborn offspring of a beast that belongs to you; the males shall be the LORD's.
verses.13:13: Every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck; and every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem.
verses.13:14: And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, 'What is this?' that you shall say to him, 'By strength of hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
verses.13:15: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh hardened himself against letting us go, that the LORD slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man and the firstborn of beast. Therefore I sacrifice to the LORD all males that open the womb, but every firstborn of my sons I redeem.'
verses.13:16: And it shall be a sign upon your hand and frontlets between your eyes, for by strength of hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt."
verses.13:17: Now it came to pass, when Pharaoh had sent the people away, that God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, "Lest the people change their minds when they see war, and return to Egypt."
verses.13:18: So God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea; and the children of Israel went up in battle array out of the land of Egypt.
verses.13:19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had placed the children of Israel under a solemn oath, saying, "God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here with you."
verses.13:20: Then they journeyed from Succoth and encamped at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.
verses.13:21: And the LORD went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them along the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that they might travel by day and by night.
verses.13:22: The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart from before the people.
verses.14:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.14:2: "Speak to the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Zephon; directly opposite it you shall encamp by the sea.
verses.14:3: For Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, 'They are entangled in the land; the wilderness has shut them in.'
verses.14:4: And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, so that he will pursue them; and I will gain honor over Pharaoh and over all his host, and the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD." And they did so.
verses.14:5: Now it was told to the king of Egypt that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and his servants was turned against the people, and they said, "What is this that we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?"
verses.14:6: So he made ready his chariot and took his people with him.
verses.14:7: And he took six hundred choice chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, with captains over every one of them.
verses.14:8: And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Israel; and the children of Israel went out with a high hand.
verses.14:9: So the Egyptians pursued after them and overtook them encamped beside the sea—all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, his horsemen, and his host—by Pi Hahiroth, before Baal Zephon.
verses.14:10: And when Pharaoh drew near, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; so they were exceedingly afraid, and the children of Israel cried out to the LORD.
verses.14:11: Then they said to Moses, "Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness? What is this that you have done to us, bringing us out of Egypt?
verses.14:12: Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, 'Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians'? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than that we should die in the wilderness."
verses.14:13: And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear; stand firm and see the salvation of the LORD, which He will work for you today. For as for the Egyptians whom you see today, you shall never see them again forever.
verses.14:14: The LORD shall fight for you, and you shall be silent."
verses.14:15: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Why do you cry out to Me? Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward.
verses.14:16: And as for you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it; and the children of Israel shall go into the midst of the sea on dry ground.
verses.14:17: And as for Me, behold, I will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they shall enter after them; and I will gain honor over Pharaoh and over all his host, over his chariots and over his horsemen.
verses.14:18: Then the Egyptians shall know that I am the LORD, when I have gained honor over Pharaoh, over his chariots, and over his horsemen."
verses.14:19: And the Angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them.
verses.14:20: So it came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud and the darkness, yet it gave light through the night, so that the one did not come near the other all the night.
verses.14:21: Then Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
verses.14:22: And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea on the dry ground, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
verses.14:23: Then the Egyptians pursued and went in after them—all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen—into the midst of the sea.
verses.14:24: And it came to pass in the morning watch that the LORD looked down upon the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and cloud, and He threw the camp of the Egyptians into confusion.
verses.14:25: And He took off their chariot wheels, so that they drove them with difficulty; and the Egyptians said, "Let us flee from before Israel, for the LORD is fighting for them against the Egyptians."
verses.14:26: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may return upon the Egyptians, upon their chariots, and upon their horsemen."
verses.14:27: So Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and as morning appeared, the sea returned to its full flow while the Egyptians were fleeing into it; thus the LORD overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.
verses.14:28: And the waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, even all the host of Pharaoh that had entered the sea after them; not so much as one of them remained.
verses.14:29: But the children of Israel walked upon dry ground in the midst of the sea, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
verses.14:30: Thus the LORD saved Israel on that day out of the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the seashore.
verses.14:31: And Israel saw the great power that the LORD had exercised against the Egyptians; so the people feared the LORD, and believed in the LORD and in His servant Moses.
verses.15:1: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to the LORD, and they spoke, saying, "I will sing to the LORD, for He is gloriously exalted; the horse and its rider He has cast into the sea.
verses.15:2: My strength and my song is the LORD, and He has become salvation to me; this is my God, and I will extol Him, the God of my father, and I will exalt Him.
verses.15:3: The LORD is a man of battle; the LORD is His name.
verses.15:4: The chariots of Pharaoh and his host He has hurled into the sea, and the choicest of his captains were sunk in the Red Sea.
verses.15:5: The deeps have covered them; they went down into the depths like a stone.
verses.15:6: Your right hand, O LORD, is glorious in might; Your right hand, O LORD, shatters the foe.
verses.15:7: And in the abundance of Your majesty You tear down those who rise against You; You send forth Your fierce wrath, and it devours them like stubble.
verses.15:8: And by the blast of Your nostrils the waters were heaped up; the flowing floods stood firm like a wall, and the deeps congealed in the heart of the sea.
verses.15:9: The enemy said, 'I will pursue, I will overtake, I will apportion the spoil; my soul shall have its fill of them; I will unsheathe my sword, and my hand shall dispossess them.'
verses.15:10: You blew with Your wind, and the sea covered them; they plunged like lead into the mighty waters.
verses.15:11: Who is like You among the gods, O LORD? Who is like You, majestic in holiness, awesome in praises, working wonders?
verses.15:12: You stretched forth Your right hand, and the earth swallowed them up.
verses.15:13: In Your lovingkindness You have led forth the people whom You redeemed; in Your strength You have guided them to the abode of Your holiness.
verses.15:14: The peoples have heard, and they tremble; pangs of anguish have seized the inhabitants of Philistia.
verses.15:15: Then the chieftains of Edom were terrified; trembling lays hold on the mighty men of Moab; all the inhabitants of Canaan have melted away.
verses.15:16: Terror and dread shall fall upon them; by the greatness of Your arm they shall be still as stone, until Your people pass over, O LORD, until the people whom You have acquired pass over.
verses.15:17: You will bring them in and plant them upon the mountain of Your inheritance, the established place You have made for Your dwelling, O LORD, the sanctuary, O Lord, which Your hands have founded.
verses.15:18: The LORD shall reign as King forever and ever."
verses.15:19: For Pharaoh's horses went into the sea with his chariots and his horsemen, and the LORD turned back the waters of the sea upon them; yet the children of Israel walked upon dry ground in the midst of the sea.
verses.15:20: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, took the timbrel in her hand, and all the women went forth after her with timbrels and with dances.
verses.15:21: And Miriam answered them in song, "Sing to the LORD, for He is gloriously exalted; the horse and its rider He has cast into the sea."
verses.15:22: Then Moses led Israel onward from the Red Sea, and they went out into the Wilderness of Shur; and they traveled three days in the wilderness and found no water.
verses.15:23: And they came to Marah, yet they could not drink the waters of Marah, for they were bitter; therefore its name was called Marah.
verses.15:24: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, "What shall we drink?"
verses.15:25: So he cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree; and he cast it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There He appointed for them a statute and an ordinance, and there He tested them,
verses.15:26: and He said, "If you will diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His eyes, and give ear to His commandments, and keep all His statutes, none of the diseases that I laid upon Egypt will I lay upon you; for I am the LORD who heals you."
verses.15:27: Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and they encamped there beside the waters.
verses.16:1: And they set out from Elim, and the whole congregation of the children of Israel came to the Wilderness of Sin, which lies between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departure from the land of Egypt.
verses.16:2: Then the whole congregation of the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron in the wilderness.
verses.16:3: And the children of Israel said to them, "If only we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat beside the pots of meat and ate bread to fullness! For you have brought us out into this wilderness to put this entire assembly to death with hunger."
verses.16:4: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather each day's portion in its day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in My law or not.
verses.16:5: And it shall be on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, that it shall be twice as much as what they gather day by day."
verses.16:6: Then Moses and Aaron said to all the children of Israel, "At evening you shall know that the LORD has brought you out of the land of Egypt,
verses.16:7: and in the morning you shall behold the glory of the LORD, for He has heard your murmurings against the LORD; and what are we, that you murmur against us?"
verses.16:8: And Moses said, "When the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and bread in the morning to fullness, it is because the LORD has heard your murmurings that you murmur against Him. And what are we? Your murmurings are not against us, but against the LORD."
verses.16:9: Then Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole congregation of the children of Israel, 'Draw near before the LORD, for He has heard your murmurings.'"
verses.16:10: And it came to pass, as Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of the children of Israel, that they turned toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud.
verses.16:11: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.16:12: "I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel. Speak to them, saying, 'At twilight you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread; and you shall know that I am the LORD your God.'"
verses.16:13: And it came to pass in the evening that quail came up and covered the camp; and in the morning a layer of dew lay all around the camp.
verses.16:14: And when the layer of dew lifted, behold, upon the face of the wilderness was a fine, flaky substance, as fine as frost upon the earth.
verses.16:15: When the children of Israel saw it, they said one to another, "What is it?" for they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, "This is the bread that the LORD has given you for food.
verses.16:16: This is the word that the LORD has commanded: Gather of it, every man according to what he eats, an omer per head according to the number of your souls; every man shall take for those who are in his tent."
verses.16:17: And the children of Israel did so, and they gathered, some more and some less.
verses.16:18: And when they measured it with an omer, the one who gathered much had no excess, and the one who gathered little had no lack; every man had gathered according to what he could eat.
verses.16:19: And Moses said to them, "Let no man leave any of it until morning."
verses.16:20: Yet they did not heed Moses, and some men left part of it until morning; and it bred worms and became foul, and Moses was angry with them.
verses.16:21: So they gathered it morning by morning, every man according to what he could eat; and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
verses.16:22: And it came to pass on the sixth day that they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each person; and all the rulers of the congregation came and reported it to Moses.
verses.16:23: Then he said to them, "This is what the LORD has spoken: Tomorrow is a solemn rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. Bake what you will bake, and boil what you will boil; and all that remains over, lay up for yourselves to be kept until morning."
verses.16:24: So they laid it up until morning, as Moses had commanded; and it did not become foul, nor was there any worm in it.
verses.16:25: And Moses said, "Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the LORD; today you shall not find it in the field.
verses.16:26: Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there shall be none."
verses.16:27: And it came to pass on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, yet they found none.
verses.16:28: Then the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you refuse to keep My commandments and My laws?
verses.16:29: See! Because the LORD has given you the Sabbath, on the sixth day He gives you bread for two days. Abide, every man in his place; let no man go forth from his place on the seventh day."
verses.16:30: So the people rested on the seventh day.
verses.16:31: And the house of Israel called its name manna; and it was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like flat wafers made with honey.
verses.16:32: Then Moses said, "This is the word that the LORD has commanded: 'A full omer of it shall be kept throughout your generations, that they may see the bread with which I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.'"
verses.16:33: And Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put a full omer of manna into it, and lay it up before the LORD, to be kept throughout your generations."
verses.16:34: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron laid it up before the Testimony to be kept.
verses.16:35: And the children of Israel ate the manna forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
verses.16:36: Now an omer is one-tenth of an ephah.
verses.17:1: Then the whole congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the Wilderness of Sin by their stages, according to the command of the LORD, and encamped at Rephidim; and there was no water for the people to drink.
verses.17:2: Therefore the people contended with Moses and said, "Give us water, that we may drink." And Moses said to them, "Why do you contend with me? Why do you test the LORD?"
verses.17:3: And the people thirsted there for water, and the people murmured against Moses and said, "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt, to kill me and my children and my livestock with thirst?"
verses.17:4: So Moses cried out to the LORD, saying, "What shall I do with this people? Yet a little while, and they will stone me!"
verses.17:5: And the LORD said to Moses, "Pass on before the people, and take with you some of the elders of Israel. Take also in your hand your rod, with which you struck the Nile, and go.
verses.17:6: Behold, I will stand before you there upon the rock in Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it, that the people may drink." And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
verses.17:7: And he called the name of that place Massah and Meribah, because of the contention of the children of Israel, and because they tested the LORD, saying, "Is the LORD in our midst, or not?"
verses.17:8: Then Amalek came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.
verses.17:9: And Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us, and go out and fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand upon the summit of the hill with the rod of God in my hand."
verses.17:10: So Joshua did as Moses had spoken to him, to fight against Amalek. And Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the summit of the hill.
verses.17:11: And it came to pass, whenever Moses lifted up his hand, Israel prevailed; and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek prevailed.
verses.17:12: Now the hands of Moses grew heavy; so they took a stone and placed it beneath him, and he sat upon it. And Aaron and Hur upheld his hands, one on this side and one on the other side; thus his hands remained steady until the going down of the sun.
verses.17:13: And Joshua overwhelmed Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
verses.17:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this as a memorial in the book and rehearse it in the hearing of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from beneath heaven."
verses.17:15: And Moses built an altar and called its name The-LORD-Is-My-Banner;
verses.17:16: for he said, "Because a hand is upon the throne of the LORD, the LORD shall have war against Amalek from generation to generation."
verses.18:1: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard of all that God had done for Moses and for Israel His people—how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
verses.18:2: Then Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took Zipporah, the wife of Moses, after he had sent her away,
verses.18:3: along with her two sons, of whom the name of the one was Gershom, for he had said, "I have been a sojourner in a foreign land,"
verses.18:4: and the name of the other was Eliezer, meaning, "The God of my father was my help, and He delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh."
verses.18:5: So Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, came with his sons and his wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was encamped at the mountain of God.
verses.18:6: And he said to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, together with your wife and her two sons with her."
verses.18:7: Then Moses went out to meet his father-in-law, bowed down, and kissed him. And they asked one another of their welfare, and went into the tent.
verses.18:8: And Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to Egypt for the sake of Israel, all the hardship that had come upon them along the way, and how the LORD had delivered them.
verses.18:9: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the LORD had done for Israel, whom He had delivered out of the hand of Egypt.
verses.18:10: And Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you out of the hand of Egypt and out of the hand of Pharaoh, and who has delivered the people from beneath the hand of Egypt.
verses.18:11: Now I know that the LORD is greater than all the gods, even in the very matter in which they dealt arrogantly against them."
verses.18:12: Then Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. And Aaron came, with all the elders of Israel, to eat bread with the father-in-law of Moses before God.
verses.18:13: And it came to pass on the next day that Moses sat to judge the people; and the people stood before Moses from the morning until the evening.
verses.18:14: Now when the father-in-law of Moses saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this thing that you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning until evening?"
verses.18:15: And Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
verses.18:16: Whenever they have a dispute, they come to me, and I judge between a man and his neighbor; and I make known the statutes of God and His laws."
verses.18:17: Then the father-in-law of Moses said to him, "The thing that you are doing is not good.
verses.18:18: You will surely wear away, both you and this people who are with you; for the matter is too heavy for you—you are not able to perform it by yourself.
verses.18:19: Now heed my voice; I will counsel you, and God shall be with you: represent the people before God, and bring the matters to God.
verses.18:20: And you shall instruct them in the statutes and the laws, and make known to them the way in which they must walk and the work which they must do.
verses.18:21: Moreover you shall select from all the people capable men, who fear God, men of truth, hating unjust gain; and appoint such over them to be rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
verses.18:22: And let them judge the people at all times; and it shall be that every great matter they shall bring to you, while every small matter they themselves shall judge. Thus lighten the burden from yourself, and they shall bear it with you.
verses.18:23: If you do this thing, and God so commands you, then you will be able to endure, and all this people also will go to their place in peace."
verses.18:24: So Moses heeded the voice of his father-in-law and did all that he had spoken.
verses.18:25: And Moses chose capable men out of all Israel, and appointed them as heads over the people—rulers of thousands, rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens.
verses.18:26: So they judged the people at all times: the difficult cases they brought to Moses, while every small matter they themselves judged.
verses.18:27: Then Moses sent his father-in-law on his way, and he departed to his own land.
verses.19:1: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out from the land of Egypt, on that very day they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.
verses.19:2: For they had departed from Rephidim, and had come to the Wilderness of Sinai, and encamped in the wilderness; and Israel encamped there before the mountain.
verses.19:3: And Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, "Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob, and declare to the children of Israel:
verses.19:4: 'You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt, and how I bore you upon the wings of eagles and brought you to Myself.
verses.19:5: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be My own treasured possession above all peoples, for all the earth is Mine;
verses.19:6: and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel."
verses.19:7: So Moses came and summoned the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which the LORD had commanded him.
