verses.19:8: And all the people answered together and said, "All that the LORD has spoken we will do." So Moses brought back the words of the people to the LORD.
verses.19:9: And the LORD said to Moses, "Behold, I am coming to you in the dense cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and may also believe in you forever." Then Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.
verses.19:10: And the LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments.
verses.19:11: And let them be ready for the third day; for on the third day the LORD will come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai.
verses.19:12: You shall set bounds for the people all around, saying, 'Take heed to yourselves that you do not go up on the mountain or touch its border; whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.
verses.19:13: No hand shall touch him, for he shall surely be stoned or surely shot through; whether beast or man, he shall not live.' When the trumpet sounds a long blast, they shall come up to the mountain."
verses.19:14: So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people, and they washed their garments.
verses.19:15: And he said to the people, "Be ready for the third day; do not go near a woman."
verses.19:16: And it came to pass on the third day, when morning broke, that there were thunderings and lightnings, and a heavy cloud upon the mountain, and the sound of a trumpet exceedingly loud; so that all the people who were in the camp trembled.
verses.19:17: And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their stand at the foot of the mountain.
verses.19:18: Now Mount Sinai was altogether in smoke, because the LORD had descended upon it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.
verses.19:19: And as the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him by a voice.
verses.19:20: Then the LORD came down upon Mount Sinai, to the summit of the mountain; and the LORD called Moses to the summit of the mountain, and Moses went up.
verses.19:21: And the LORD said to Moses, "Go down and solemnly warn the people, lest they break through to the LORD to gaze, and many of them perish.
verses.19:22: Also let the priests who draw near to the LORD consecrate themselves, lest the LORD break out against them."
verses.19:23: And Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai; for You Yourself warned us, saying, 'Set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it.'"
verses.19:24: Then the LORD said to him, "Go, get down, and then come up, you and Aaron with you; but do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest He break out against them."
verses.19:25: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
verses.20:1: Now God spoke all these words, saying:
verses.20:2: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you forth from the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
verses.20:3: You shall not have other gods before My presence.
verses.20:4: You shall not make for yourself a graven image, nor any likeness of what is in the heavens above, or in the earth beneath, or in the waters under the earth.
verses.20:5: You shall not bow down before them nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon children, to the third and the fourth generation of those who hate Me,
verses.20:6: yet showing lovingkindness to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments.
verses.20:7: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not acquit the one who takes His name in vain.
verses.20:8: Remember the Sabbath day, to sanctify it.
verses.20:9: Six days you shall labor and perform all your work,
verses.20:10: but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God; you shall not do any work—neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor your livestock, nor your sojourner who is within your gates.
verses.20:11: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and everything that is in them, and He rested on the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it.
verses.20:12: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be prolonged upon the land which the LORD your God gives you.
verses.20:16: You shall not testify as a false witness against your neighbor.
verses.20:17: You shall not covet your neighbor's house; you shall not covet your neighbor's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that belongs to your neighbor."
verses.20:18: And all the people perceived the thunderings and the lightning flashes, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw it, they trembled and stood far off.
verses.20:19: Then they said to Moses, "You yourself speak with us, and we will hear; but do not let God speak with us, lest we die."
verses.20:20: And Moses said to the people, "Do not fear, for God has come in order to test you, and so that the fear of Him may be before you, that you may not sin."
verses.20:21: So the people remained standing at a distance, while Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.
verses.20:22: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Thus you shall say to the children of Israel: 'You yourselves have seen that from heaven I have spoken with you.
verses.20:23: You shall not make gods beside Me—gods of silver and gods of gold you shall not make for yourselves.
verses.20:24: An altar of earth you shall make for Me, and upon it you shall sacrifice your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your flocks and your herds. In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
verses.20:25: And if you make for Me an altar of stones, you shall not build them of hewn stone; for if you lift your chisel upon it, you will profane it.
verses.20:26: Nor shall you ascend by steps to My altar, so that your nakedness may not be uncovered upon it.'"
verses.21:1: Now these are the ordinances that you shall set before them:
verses.21:2: When you buy a Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve, and in the seventh he shall go forth free, without payment.
verses.21:3: If he enters alone, he shall depart alone; if he is the husband of a wife, then his wife shall go out with him.
verses.21:4: If his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the woman and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall depart alone.
verses.21:5: But if the servant solemnly declares, "I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free,"
verses.21:6: then his master shall bring him before God, and bring him to the door or to the doorpost; and his master shall pierce his ear with an awl, and he shall serve him forever.
verses.21:7: And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant, she shall not depart as the menservants depart.
verses.21:8: If she is displeasing in the eyes of her master, who has designated her for himself, then he shall allow her to be redeemed; he shall have no authority to sell her to a foreign people, since he has dealt faithlessly with her.
verses.21:9: And if he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her according to the rights of daughters.
verses.21:10: If he takes another woman for himself, he shall not diminish her sustenance, her clothing, or her marital rights.
verses.21:11: And if he does not perform these three things for her, then she shall go out free, without payment of money.
verses.21:12: Whoever strikes a man so that he dies shall surely be put to death.
verses.21:13: Yet if he did not lie in wait, but God delivered him into his hand, then I will appoint for you a place to which he may flee.
verses.21:14: But if a man acts willfully against his neighbor to slay him by treachery, you shall take him from My altar, that he may die.
verses.21:15: And whoever strikes his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
verses.21:16: And whoever curses his father or his mother shall surely be put to death.
verses.21:17: And whoever steals a man and sells him, or if he is found in his hand, shall surely be put to death.
verses.21:18: And when men contend with one another, and one strikes his neighbor with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but takes to his bed,
verses.21:19: if he rises again and walks outdoors leaning on his staff, then the one who struck him shall be cleared of guilt; only he shall compensate for his lost time and ensure that he is thoroughly healed.
verses.21:20: And if a man strikes his manservant or his maidservant with a rod, and the servant dies under his hand, he shall surely be avenged.
verses.21:21: Nevertheless, if he endures a day or two, he shall not be avenged, for he is his property.
verses.21:22: And when men strive together and strike a pregnant woman, so that her children come forth, yet no harm ensues, he shall surely be fined according to what the woman's husband lays upon him, and he shall pay as the judges determine.
verses.21:23: But if harm ensues, then you shall give life for life,
verses.21:24: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
verses.21:25: burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
verses.21:26: And if a man strikes the eye of his manservant or the eye of his maidservant and destroys it, he shall release him free on account of his eye.
verses.21:27: And if he knocks out the tooth of his manservant or the tooth of his maidservant, he shall release him free on account of his tooth.
verses.21:28: And if an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox shall surely be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; yet the owner of the ox shall be held blameless.
verses.21:29: But if the ox was prone to gore in times past, and its owner had been warned, yet he did not restrain it, and it puts to death a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death.
verses.21:30: If a ransom is laid upon him, then he shall pay for the redemption of his life whatever is laid upon him.
verses.21:31: Whether it gores a son or gores a daughter, according to this same ordinance it shall be done to him.
verses.21:32: If the ox gores a manservant or a maidservant, he shall pay thirty shekels of silver to his master, and the ox shall be stoned.
verses.21:33: And if a man opens a pit, or if a man digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
verses.21:34: the owner of the pit shall make restitution; he shall repay silver to its owner, and the dead animal shall belong to him.
verses.21:35: And if a man's ox strikes his neighbor's ox so that it dies, then they shall sell the living ox and divide its price, and they shall also divide the dead one.
verses.21:36: Or if it was known that the ox was prone to gore in times past, and its owner did not restrain it, he shall surely make restitution, ox for ox, and the dead animal shall belong to him.
verses.21:37: If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall restore five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
verses.22:1: If a thief is found breaking in, and he is struck so that he dies, there shall be no bloodguilt on his account.
verses.22:2: If the sun has risen upon him, there shall be bloodguilt on his account. He shall surely make restitution; if he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
verses.22:3: If the stolen property is indeed found alive in his hand, whether ox or donkey or sheep, he shall repay double.
verses.22:4: If a man causes a field or vineyard to be grazed over, and lets his livestock loose so that it grazes in the field of another, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and from the best of his own vineyard.
verses.22:5: If fire breaks out and catches in thorns, so that stacked grain, or standing grain, or the field is consumed, the one who kindled the fire shall surely make restitution.
verses.22:6: If a man entrusts money or goods to his neighbor for safekeeping, and it is stolen from the man's house, if the thief is found, he shall repay double.
verses.22:7: If the thief is not found, then the owner of the house shall come near before God, to determine whether he has laid his hand upon his neighbor's property.
verses.22:8: For every matter of transgression—whether concerning an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or any lost thing of which one says, "This is it"—the case of both parties shall come before God; the one whom God condemns shall repay double to his neighbor.
verses.22:9: If a man entrusts to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any beast for safekeeping, and it dies, or is injured, or is driven away with no one seeing it,
verses.22:10: then an oath of the LORD shall be between them both that he has not laid his hand upon his neighbor's property; and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not make restitution.
verses.22:11: But if it is indeed stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
verses.22:12: If it is indeed torn to pieces, let him bring it as evidence; he shall not make restitution for what was torn.
verses.22:13: And if a man borrows anything from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, he shall surely make restitution.
verses.22:14: If its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution; if it was hired, it came for its hire.
verses.22:15: And if a man entices a virgin who is not betrothed, and lies with her, he shall surely pay the bride-price for her to be his wife.
verses.22:16: If her father utterly refuses to give her to him, he shall weigh out silver equal to the bride-price of virgins.
verses.22:17: You shall not permit a sorceress to live.
verses.22:18: Whoever lies with a beast shall surely be put to death.
verses.22:19: Whoever sacrifices to any god, except to the LORD alone, shall be devoted to destruction.
verses.22:20: You shall neither wrong a sojourner nor oppress him, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
verses.22:21: You shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child.
verses.22:22: If you afflict them in any way, and they cry out at all to Me, I will surely hear their cry;
verses.22:23: and My wrath shall burn hot, and I will slay you with the sword; and your wives shall become widows, and your children fatherless.
verses.22:24: If you lend money to any of My people who are poor among you, you shall not act toward him like a creditor, nor shall you impose interest upon him.
verses.22:25: If you ever take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, you shall return it to him before the sun goes down.
verses.22:26: For that is his only covering; it is his garment for his skin. In what shall he sleep? And it shall come to pass, when he cries out to Me, that I will hear, for I am gracious.
verses.22:27: You shall not revile God, nor curse a ruler among your people.
verses.22:28: You shall not delay to offer the fullness of your harvest and the outflow of your presses; the firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me.
verses.22:29: Likewise you shall do with your oxen and your sheep: seven days it shall remain with its mother; on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.
verses.22:30: And you shall be holy men to Me; you shall not eat any flesh torn by beasts in the field, but you shall cast it to the dogs.
verses.23:1: You shall not spread a false report; do not join your hand with the wicked to be a malicious witness.
verses.23:2: You shall not follow a multitude to do evil, nor shall you testify in a dispute so as to side with a multitude to pervert justice.
verses.23:3: Nor shall you show partiality to a poor man in his dispute.
verses.23:4: If you come upon your enemy's ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him.
verses.23:5: If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying under its burden, and you would refrain from helping him, you shall surely assist him with it.
verses.23:6: You shall not pervert the justice due to your poor in his dispute.
verses.23:7: Keep far from a false charge, and do not slay the innocent and the righteous, for I will not acquit the wicked.
verses.23:8: And you shall take no bribe, for a bribe blinds the clear-sighted and subverts the words of the righteous.
verses.23:9: Also you shall not oppress a sojourner, for you yourselves know the soul of a sojourner, since you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.
verses.23:10: Six years you shall sow your land and gather in its produce,
verses.23:11: but in the seventh year you shall let it rest and lie fallow, that the needy of your people may eat; and what they leave, the beasts of the field may eat. In like manner you shall do with your vineyard and with your olive grove.
verses.23:12: Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your maidservant and the sojourner may be refreshed.
verses.23:13: And in all that I have spoken to you, take heed; make no mention of the name of other gods, nor let it be heard from your mouth.
verses.23:14: Three times in the year you shall keep a feast to Me:
verses.23:15: You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread—seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in it you came out of Egypt—and none shall appear before Me empty-handed.
verses.23:16: Also you shall keep the Feast of Harvest, the firstfruits of your labors which you have sown in the field; and the Feast of Ingathering at the close of the year, when you gather in the fruit of your labors from the field.
verses.23:17: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Master, the LORD.
verses.23:18: You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with leavened bread, nor shall the fat of My feast remain until morning.
verses.23:19: The choicest of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring into the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
verses.23:20: Behold, I send an angel before you to guard you along the way and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
verses.23:21: Pay careful heed to him and obey his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgression, since My name is in him.
verses.23:22: But if you diligently obey his voice and do all that I speak, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to your adversaries.
verses.23:23: For My angel shall go before you and bring you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; and I will blot them out.
verses.23:24: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do according to their deeds; rather, you shall utterly overthrow them and completely shatter their sacred pillars.
verses.23:25: So you shall serve the LORD your God, and He shall bless your bread and your water; and I will remove sickness from your midst.
verses.23:26: None shall miscarry or be barren in your land; I will fulfill the number of your days.
verses.23:27: I will send My terror before you, and I will throw into confusion all the people among whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
verses.23:28: And I will send hornets before you, which shall drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites, and the Hittites from before you.
verses.23:29: I will not drive them out from before you in a single year, lest the land become desolate and the beasts of the field become too numerous for you.
verses.23:30: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have increased and inherit the land.
verses.23:31: And I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.
verses.23:32: You shall make no covenant with them, nor with their gods.
verses.23:33: They shall not dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against Me; for if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.
verses.24:1: Now He said to Moses, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and worship from afar.
verses.24:2: And Moses alone shall draw near to the LORD, yet they shall not draw near, nor shall the people come up with him."
verses.24:3: Then Moses came and recounted to the people all the words of the LORD and all the judgments. And all the people answered with one voice and said, "All the words which the LORD has spoken we will do."
verses.24:4: And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. And he rose early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and twelve pillars for the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.24:5: Then he sent the young men of the children of Israel, who offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls as peace offerings to the LORD.
verses.24:6: And Moses took half of the blood and put it in the basins, and half of the blood he sprinkled upon the altar.
verses.24:7: Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it in the hearing of the people. And they said, "All that the LORD has spoken we will do, and we will obey."
verses.24:8: And Moses took the blood and sprinkled it upon the people, and said, "Behold, the blood of the covenant which the LORD has made with you concerning all these words."
verses.24:9: Then Moses went up, together with Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel.
verses.24:10: And they saw the God of Israel. And beneath His feet there was as it were a pavement of sapphire stone, like the very heavens in clarity.
verses.24:11: Yet against the nobles of the children of Israel He did not stretch out His hand; indeed, they beheld God, and they ate and drank.
verses.24:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Come up to Me on the mountain and remain there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, and the law and the commandment which I have written, to instruct them."
verses.24:13: So Moses arose with Joshua his attendant, and Moses went up to the mountain of God.
verses.24:14: And to the elders he said, "Wait for us in this place until we return to you. And behold, Aaron and Hur are with you; whoever has a dispute, let him draw near to them."
verses.24:15: Then Moses went up into the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
verses.24:16: Now the glory of the LORD dwelt upon Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. And on the seventh day He called to Moses from the midst of the cloud.
verses.24:17: And the appearance of the glory of the LORD was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain in the sight of the children of Israel.
verses.24:18: So Moses entered into the midst of the cloud and went up into the mountain. And Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
verses.25:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.25:2: "Speak to the children of Israel, that they bring Me an offering. From every man whose heart prompts him willingly you shall receive My offering.
verses.25:3: And this is the offering which you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
verses.25:4: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, and goat hair;
verses.25:5: ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
verses.25:7: onyx stones, and stones for setting in the ephod and in the breastplate.
verses.25:8: And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst.
verses.25:9: According to all that I am showing you—the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings—just so you shall make it.
verses.25:10: And they shall make an ark of acacia wood; two and a half cubits shall be its length, a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
verses.25:11: And you shall overlay it with pure gold; inside and outside you shall overlay it, and you shall make upon it a molding of gold all around.
verses.25:12: And you shall cast four rings of gold for it and set them upon its four feet—two rings on its one side, and two rings on its other side.
verses.25:13: And you shall make poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
verses.25:14: And you shall insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark by them.
verses.25:15: The poles shall remain in the rings of the ark; they shall not be removed from it.
verses.25:16: And you shall place into the ark the Testimony which I will give you.
verses.25:17: You shall also make a mercy seat of pure gold; two and a half cubits shall be its length, and a cubit and a half its width.
verses.25:18: And you shall make two cherubim of gold; of hammered work you shall make them at the two ends of the mercy seat.
verses.25:19: Make one cherub at the one end and one cherub at the other end; of one piece with the mercy seat you shall make the cherubim at its two ends.
verses.25:20: And the cherubim shall spread out their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces one toward the other; toward the mercy seat shall the faces of the cherubim be.
verses.25:21: And you shall set the mercy seat upon the top of the ark, and in the ark you shall place the Testimony which I will give you.
verses.25:22: And there I will meet with you, and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim which are upon the ark of the Testimony, of all that I will command you for the children of Israel.
verses.25:23: You shall also make a table of acacia wood; two cubits shall be its length, a cubit its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
verses.25:24: And you shall overlay it with pure gold, and make for it a molding of gold all around.
verses.25:25: And you shall make for it a frame of a handbreadth all around, and you shall make a molding of gold for its frame all around.
verses.25:26: And you shall make for it four rings of gold, and attach the rings to the four corners that are on its four legs.
verses.25:27: Close to the frame the rings shall be, as holders for the poles to carry the table.
verses.25:28: And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold, that the table may be carried with them.
verses.25:29: You shall also make its plates, its dishes, its pitchers, and its bowls with which drink offerings are poured; of pure gold you shall make them.
verses.25:30: And you shall set the bread of the Presence upon the table before Me continually.
verses.25:31: And you shall make a lampstand of pure gold; of hammered work shall the lampstand be made. Its base and its shaft, its cups, its calyxes, and its blossoms shall be of one piece with it.
verses.25:32: And six branches shall extend from its sides: three branches of the lampstand out of its one side, and three branches of the lampstand out of its other side.
verses.25:33: Three cups shaped like almond blossoms shall be on the one branch, with a calyx and a blossom, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the next branch, with a calyx and a blossom—so for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
verses.25:34: And on the lampstand itself there shall be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its calyxes and its blossoms.
verses.25:35: And there shall be a calyx beneath two of the branches of one piece with it, and a calyx beneath two of the branches of one piece with it, and a calyx beneath two of the branches of one piece with it—according to the six branches extending from the lampstand.
verses.25:36: Their calyxes and their branches shall be of one piece with it; the whole of it shall be one hammered piece of pure gold.
verses.25:37: You shall also make seven lamps for it, and they shall mount its lamps so that they shed light upon the space in front of it.
verses.25:38: And its tongs and its trays shall be of pure gold.
verses.25:39: Of a talent of pure gold it shall be made, along with all these utensils.
verses.25:40: And see that you make them according to their pattern which is being shown to you on the mountain."
verses.26:1: Moreover, you shall make the tabernacle of ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; with cherubim, the work of a skillful designer, you shall make them.
verses.26:2: The length of each curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; all the curtains shall be of one measure.
verses.26:3: Five of the curtains shall be coupled one to another, and the other five curtains shall be coupled one to another.
verses.26:4: And you shall make loops of blue upon the edge of the one curtain, at the end of the first set; and likewise you shall make them upon the edge of the outermost curtain in the second set.
verses.26:5: Fifty loops you shall make on the one curtain, and fifty loops you shall make on the end of the curtain that is in the second set, the loops standing directly opposite one another.
verses.26:6: And you shall make fifty clasps of gold, and couple the curtains one to another with the clasps, and the tabernacle shall be one.
verses.26:7: You shall also make curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle; eleven curtains you shall make them.
verses.26:8: The length of each curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain four cubits; the eleven curtains shall all be of one measure.
verses.26:9: And you shall couple five of the curtains by themselves and six of the curtains by themselves, and you shall fold back the sixth curtain at the front of the tent.
verses.26:10: And you shall make fifty loops upon the edge of the one outermost curtain in the first set, and fifty loops upon the edge of the curtain of the second set.
verses.26:11: And you shall make fifty clasps of bronze, and put the clasps into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one.
verses.26:12: And as for the overhanging remnant of the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that remains shall hang over the rear of the tabernacle.
verses.26:13: And the cubit on the one side and the cubit on the other side, of that which remains in the length of the curtains of the tent, shall hang down over the sides of the tabernacle, on this side and on that side, to cover it.
verses.26:14: You shall also make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of fine leather above that.
verses.26:15: And for the tabernacle you shall make the boards of acacia wood, standing upright.
verses.26:16: Ten cubits shall be the length of each board, and a cubit and a half shall be the width of each board.
verses.26:17: Two tenons shall be in each board, fitted one to another; thus you shall make for all the boards of the tabernacle.
verses.26:18: And you shall make the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side, southward.
verses.26:19: And you shall make forty sockets of silver beneath the twenty boards: two sockets beneath one board for its two tenons, and two sockets beneath the next board for its two tenons.
verses.26:20: And for the second side of the tabernacle, on the north side, there shall be twenty boards,
verses.26:21: and their forty sockets of silver: two sockets beneath one board, and two sockets beneath the next board.
verses.26:22: And for the far end of the tabernacle, westward, you shall make six boards.
verses.26:23: And two boards you shall make for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
verses.26:24: They shall be coupled together from beneath, and in the same way they shall be completely joined at the top into a single ring; thus shall it be for both of them—they shall be for the two corners.
verses.26:25: So there shall be eight boards, with their silver sockets, sixteen sockets in all: two sockets beneath one board, and two sockets beneath the next board.
verses.26:26: And you shall make bars of acacia wood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,
verses.26:27: five bars for the boards of the other side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the side of the tabernacle at the rear, westward.
verses.26:28: And the middle bar shall pass through the center of the boards from end to end.
verses.26:29: You shall overlay the boards with gold, make their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and overlay the bars with gold.
verses.26:30: And you shall erect the tabernacle according to the plan of it that was shown to you on the mountain.
verses.26:31: You shall also make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen; it shall be made with cherubim, the work of a skillful designer.
verses.26:32: And you shall hang it upon four pillars of acacia wood overlaid with gold, their hooks being of gold, set upon four sockets of silver.
verses.26:33: And you shall hang the veil beneath the clasps; then you shall bring the ark of the Testimony in there, behind the veil. And the veil shall make a separation for you between the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place.
verses.26:34: You shall set the mercy seat upon the ark of the Testimony in the Most Holy Place.
verses.26:35: And you shall place the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle; and the table you shall put on the north side.
verses.26:36: You shall also make a screen for the entrance of the tent, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
verses.26:37: And you shall make for the screen five pillars of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold; their hooks shall be of gold, and you shall cast five sockets of bronze for them.
verses.27:1: You shall also make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide—the altar shall be foursquare—and three cubits shall be its height.
verses.27:2: And you shall make its horns upon its four corners; its horns shall be of one piece with it, and you shall overlay it with bronze.
verses.27:3: You shall also make its pots to receive its ashes, and its shovels, its basins, its forks, and its firepans; all its utensils you shall make of bronze.
verses.27:4: And you shall make for it a grate, a network of bronze; and upon the network you shall make four bronze rings at its four corners.
verses.27:5: And you shall set it beneath the ledge of the altar from below, so that the network reaches halfway up the altar.
verses.27:6: And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
verses.27:7: Its poles shall be inserted into the rings, and the poles shall be on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
verses.27:8: Hollow with planks you shall make it; as it was shown to you on the mountain, so shall they make it.
verses.27:9: You shall also make the court of the tabernacle. For the south side, southward, there shall be hangings for the court of fine twisted linen, one hundred cubits long for that one side.
verses.27:10: Its pillars shall be twenty, and their twenty sockets of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
verses.27:11: Likewise for the north side along its length, there shall be hangings one hundred cubits long, and its twenty pillars and their twenty sockets of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands shall be of silver.
verses.27:12: And for the width of the court on the west side there shall be hangings of fifty cubits, with their ten pillars and their ten sockets.
verses.27:13: And the width of the court on the east side, toward the sunrise, shall be fifty cubits.
verses.27:14: The hangings on the one side of the gate shall be fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
verses.27:15: And on the other side shall be hangings of fifteen cubits, with their three pillars and their three sockets.
verses.27:16: And for the gate of the court there shall be a screen of twenty cubits, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with its four pillars and its four sockets.
verses.27:17: All the pillars around the court shall be banded with silver; their hooks shall be of silver, and their sockets of bronze.
verses.27:18: The length of the court shall be one hundred cubits, the width fifty cubits throughout, and the height five cubits, of fine twisted linen, with their sockets of bronze.
verses.27:19: All the utensils of the tabernacle for all its service, together with all its pegs and all the pegs of the court, shall be of bronze.
verses.27:20: And you shall command the children of Israel that they bring to you pure beaten olive oil for the light, to keep the lamp burning continually.
verses.27:21: In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is before the Testimony, Aaron and his sons shall tend it from evening until morning before the LORD. It shall be a perpetual statute throughout their generations, to be observed by the children of Israel.
verses.28:1: Now you, bring near to yourself Aaron your brother, and his sons with him, from the midst of the children of Israel, that he may serve as priest to Me—Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron.
verses.28:2: And you shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother, for glory and for splendor.
verses.28:3: And you shall speak to all who are wise of heart, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, that they may make the garments of Aaron to consecrate him, that he may serve as priest to Me.
verses.28:4: And these are the garments which they shall make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a checkered tunic, a turban, and a sash. Thus they shall make holy garments for Aaron your brother and for his sons, that he may serve as priest to Me.
verses.28:5: And they shall take the gold, the blue, the purple, the scarlet yarn, and the fine linen.
verses.28:6: And they shall make the ephod of gold, of blue and purple, of scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen, the work of a skillful designer.
verses.28:7: It shall have two shoulder pieces attached to it at its two edges, so that it may be joined together.
verses.28:8: And the woven waistband of the ephod, which is upon it, shall be of the same workmanship and of one piece with it: of gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
verses.28:9: And you shall take two onyx stones, and engrave upon them the names of the sons of Israel:
verses.28:10: six of their names on the one stone, and the names of the remaining six on the second stone, according to the order of their birth.
verses.28:11: With the work of a stone engraver, like the engravings of a signet, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel; you shall mount them enclosed in settings of gold.
verses.28:12: And you shall place the two stones upon the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of memorial for the sons of Israel; and Aaron shall bear their names before the LORD upon his two shoulders for a memorial.
verses.28:13: And you shall make settings of gold.
verses.28:14: And you shall make two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords of braided work, and you shall fasten the braided chains to the settings.
verses.28:15: And you shall make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skillful designer; like the workmanship of the ephod you shall make it: of gold, blue, purple, scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen you shall make it.
verses.28:16: It shall be square, folded double: a span shall be its length, and a span shall be its width.
verses.28:17: And you shall fill it with settings of stones, four rows of stones: a row of sardius, topaz, and emerald shall be the first row;
verses.28:18: and the second row shall be carbuncle, sapphire, and diamond;
verses.28:19: and the third row shall be jacinth, agate, and amethyst;
verses.28:20: and the fourth row shall be beryl, onyx, and jasper. They shall be enclosed in gold in their settings.
verses.28:21: And the stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, each one with its own name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
verses.28:22: And you shall make upon the breastpiece twisted chains of braided work, of pure gold.
verses.28:29: And you shall put the two braided cords of gold on the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece. And the two ends of the two braided cords you shall fasten to the two settings, and place them upon the shoulder pieces of the ephod at its front. So Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel in the breastpiece of judgment upon his heart, when he enters the holy place, for a memorial before the LORD continually.
verses.28:30: And you shall put in the breastpiece of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be upon the heart of Aaron when he goes in before the LORD; thus Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Israel upon his heart before the LORD continually.
verses.28:31: And you shall make the robe of the ephod wholly of blue.
verses.28:32: And there shall be an opening for the head in the midst of it; it shall have a woven border around its opening, the work of a weaver, like the opening of a coat of mail, so that it shall not be torn.
verses.28:33: And upon its hem you shall make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, around its hem on every side, and bells of gold between them all around:
verses.28:34: a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, upon the hem of the robe all around.
verses.28:35: And it shall be upon Aaron when he ministers, and its sound shall be heard when he enters the holy place before the LORD and when he comes out, so that he may not die.
verses.28:36: And you shall make a plate of pure gold, and engrave upon it, like the engravings of a signet, "Holiness to the LORD."
verses.28:37: And you shall fasten it on a cord of blue, that it may be upon the turban; upon the front of the turban it shall be.
verses.28:38: And it shall be upon the forehead of Aaron, that Aaron may bear the iniquity of the holy things which the children of Israel consecrate in all their holy gifts; and it shall be upon his forehead continually, that they may find acceptance before the LORD.
verses.28:39: And you shall weave the tunic in checkered work of fine linen, and you shall make a turban of fine linen, and a sash you shall make as the work of an embroiderer.
verses.28:40: And for the sons of Aaron you shall make tunics, and you shall make sashes for them, and headdresses you shall make for them, for glory and for splendor.
verses.28:41: And you shall clothe Aaron your brother with them, and his sons with him; and you shall anoint them, and ordain them, and consecrate them, that they may serve as priests to Me.
verses.28:42: And make for them linen undergarments to cover their nakedness; from the waist to the thighs they shall reach.
verses.28:43: And they shall be upon Aaron and upon his sons when they enter the tent of meeting, or when they approach the altar to minister in the holy place, lest they bear iniquity and die. It shall be an everlasting statute for him and for his descendants after him.
verses.29:1: And this is the thing that you shall do for them to consecrate them, that they may serve as priests to Me: take one young bull of the herd and two rams without blemish,
verses.29:2: and unleavened bread, and unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil; you shall make them of fine wheat flour.
verses.29:3: And you shall place them in one basket and bring them near in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
verses.29:4: And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.
verses.29:5: Then you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastplate, and gird him with the woven band of the ephod.
verses.29:6: And you shall set the turban upon his head, and put the holy crown upon the turban.
verses.29:7: Then you shall take the anointing oil, pour it upon his head, and anoint him.
verses.29:8: And you shall bring his sons near and clothe them with tunics.
verses.29:9: And you shall gird them with sashes, Aaron and his sons, and bind caps upon them; and the priesthood shall be theirs by a perpetual statute. Thus you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.
verses.29:10: And you shall bring the bull before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the bull.
verses.29:11: Then you shall slaughter the bull before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.29:12: And you shall take some of the blood of the bull and apply it to the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
verses.29:13: And you shall take all the fat that covers the inward parts, and the lobe upon the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is upon them, and offer them up in smoke upon the altar.
verses.29:14: But the flesh of the bull, and its hide, and its dung, you shall burn with fire outside the camp; it is a sin offering.
verses.29:15: And you shall take the one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.
verses.29:16: Then you shall slaughter the ram, and take its blood and dash it against the altar all around.
verses.29:17: And you shall cut the ram into its pieces, and wash its inward parts and its legs, and place them with its pieces and with its head.
verses.29:18: And you shall offer up the entire ram in smoke upon the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a soothing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
verses.29:19: Then you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.
verses.29:20: And you shall slaughter the ram, and take some of its blood and apply it to the lobe of the right ear of Aaron, and to the lobe of the right ear of his sons, and to the thumb of their right hand, and to the great toe of their right foot, and dash the blood against the altar all around.
verses.29:21: And you shall take some of the blood that is upon the altar, and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it upon Aaron and upon his garments, and upon his sons and upon the garments of his sons with him; so he and his garments shall be consecrated, and his sons and the garments of his sons with him.
verses.29:22: And you shall take from the ram the fat and the fat tail, the fat that covers the inward parts, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat that is upon them, and the right thigh, for it is a ram of ordination;
verses.29:23: and one loaf of bread, one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before the LORD.
verses.29:24: And you shall place all of these upon the palms of Aaron and upon the palms of his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
verses.29:25: Then you shall take them from their hands and offer them up in smoke upon the altar on top of the burnt offering, for a soothing aroma before the LORD; it is an offering made by fire to the LORD.
verses.29:26: And you shall take the breast from the ram of ordination that is for Aaron, and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD; and it shall be your portion.
verses.29:27: And you shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the heave offering, which was waved and which was lifted up from the ram of ordination, from that which is for Aaron and from that which is for his sons.
verses.29:28: And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons by a perpetual statute from the children of Israel, for it is a heave offering; and it shall be a heave offering from the children of Israel out of the sacrifices of their peace offerings, their heave offering to the LORD.
verses.29:29: And the holy garments that belong to Aaron shall be his sons' after him, to be anointed in them and to be ordained in them.
verses.29:30: Seven days shall the priest from among his sons who succeeds him wear them, when he enters the tent of meeting to minister in the holy place.
verses.29:31: And you shall take the ram of ordination and boil its flesh in a holy place.
verses.29:32: And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
verses.29:33: They shall eat those things by which atonement was made to ordain them and to consecrate them; but an outsider shall not eat of them, for they are holy.
verses.29:34: And if any of the flesh of ordination or of the bread remains until the morning, then you shall burn the remainder with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is holy.
verses.29:35: Thus you shall do to Aaron and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded you; seven days you shall ordain them.
verses.29:36: And you shall offer a bull each day as a sin offering for atonement; and you shall purify the altar when you make atonement for it, and you shall anoint it to consecrate it.
verses.29:37: Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it; and the altar shall be most holy. Whatever touches the altar shall become holy.
verses.29:38: Now this is what you shall offer upon the altar: two lambs of the first year each day continually.
verses.29:39: The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer at twilight.
verses.29:40: And a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a fourth of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a fourth of a hin of wine, shall be for the one lamb.
verses.29:41: And the second lamb you shall offer at twilight; you shall do with it according to the grain offering of the morning and according to its drink offering, for a soothing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
verses.29:42: This shall be a continual burnt offering throughout your generations at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you to speak to you there.
verses.29:43: And there I will meet with the children of Israel, and it shall be sanctified by My glory.
verses.29:44: And I will sanctify the tent of meeting and the altar; Aaron also and his sons I will sanctify to serve as priests to Me.
verses.29:45: And I will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel, and I will be their God.
verses.29:46: And they shall know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt that I might dwell in their midst; I am the LORD their God.
verses.30:1: "And you shall make an altar for the burning of incense; of acacia wood you shall make it.
verses.30:2: One cubit shall be its length and one cubit its breadth; foursquare it shall be, and two cubits shall be its height. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.
verses.30:3: You shall overlay it with pure gold, its top and its walls all around and its horns, and you shall make for it a molding of gold all around.
verses.30:4: And two rings of gold you shall make for it beneath its molding; on its two corners, upon its two sides, you shall make them, and they shall serve as holders for poles with which to bear it.
verses.30:5: And you shall make the poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.
verses.30:6: And you shall place it before the veil that is before the ark of the Testimony, before the mercy seat that is over the Testimony, where I will meet with you.
verses.30:7: Aaron shall burn fragrant incense upon it; morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.
verses.30:8: And when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight, he shall burn it, a perpetual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
verses.30:9: You shall not offer upon it strange incense, nor a burnt offering, nor a grain offering; neither shall you pour a drink offering upon it.
verses.30:10: And Aaron shall make atonement upon its horns once a year; with the blood of the sin offering of atonement he shall make atonement upon it once a year throughout your generations. It is most holy to the LORD."
verses.30:11: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.30:12: "When you take the census of the children of Israel according to their number, each man shall give a ransom for his life to the LORD when you number them, that there may be no plague among them when you number them.
verses.30:13: This is what everyone who passes over among those who are numbered shall give: half a shekel according to the shekel of the sanctuary—the shekel is twenty gerahs—half a shekel as an offering to the LORD.
verses.30:14: Everyone who passes over among those who are numbered, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the offering to the LORD.
verses.30:15: The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less, than half a shekel, when presenting the offering to the LORD to make atonement for your souls.
verses.30:16: And you shall receive the atonement silver from the children of Israel and assign it for the service of the tent of meeting, that it may be a memorial for the children of Israel before the LORD, to make atonement for your souls."
verses.30:17: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.30:18: "You shall also make a laver of bronze, and its base of bronze, for washing; and you shall set it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water into it.
verses.30:19: And Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet from it.
verses.30:20: When they enter the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water, lest they die; or when they draw near to the altar to minister, to burn an offering made by fire to the LORD.
verses.30:21: So they shall wash their hands and their feet, lest they die. And it shall be a perpetual statute for them—for him and for his descendants throughout their generations."
verses.30:22: Moreover the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.30:23: "Take also for yourself the choicest spices: five hundred shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much—two hundred and fifty shekels—of fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty shekels of aromatic cane,
verses.30:24: and five hundred shekels of cassia, measured by the shekel of the sanctuary, and a hin of olive oil.
verses.30:25: And you shall make of these a holy anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer; a holy anointing oil it shall be.
verses.30:26: With it you shall anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the Testimony,
verses.30:27: the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, and the altar of incense,
verses.30:28: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the laver and its base.
verses.30:29: You shall consecrate them, so that they shall be most holy; whatever touches them shall become holy.
verses.30:30: And you shall anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them, that they may serve Me as priests.
verses.30:31: And you shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, 'This shall be a holy anointing oil to Me throughout your generations.
verses.30:32: It shall not be poured upon the flesh of man, nor shall you make any other like it according to its composition. It is holy, and it shall be holy to you.
verses.30:33: Whoever blends any like it, or whoever puts any of it upon an outsider, shall be cut off from his people.'"
verses.30:34: And the LORD said to Moses, "Take for yourself fragrant spices—stacte, onycha, and galbanum—fragrant spices with pure frankincense; of each there shall be an equal portion.
verses.30:35: And you shall make of these an incense, a blend after the art of the perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
verses.30:36: And you shall grind some of it very fine, and place some of it before the Testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be most holy to you.
verses.30:37: And as for the incense that you shall make, you shall not make any for yourselves according to its composition; it shall be to you holy for the LORD.
verses.30:38: Whoever makes any like it to smell its fragrance shall be cut off from his people."
verses.31:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.31:2: "See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
verses.31:3: And I have filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in every kind of craftsmanship,
verses.31:4: to devise skilled designs, to work in gold, in silver, and in bronze,
verses.31:5: in the cutting of stones for setting, and in the carving of wood, to labor in every manner of workmanship.
verses.31:6: And behold, I Myself have appointed with him Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; and into the heart of all who are wise of heart I have placed wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded you:
verses.31:7: the tent of meeting, the ark for the Testimony, the mercy seat that is upon it, and all the furnishings of the tent,
verses.31:8: the table and its utensils, the pure lampstand with all its utensils, and the altar of incense,
verses.31:9: the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the laver and its base,
verses.31:10: the finely woven garments, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests,
verses.31:11: and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the holy place. According to all that I have commanded you, they shall make them."
verses.31:12: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.31:13: "And you, speak to the children of Israel, saying, 'Surely you shall keep My Sabbaths, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.
verses.31:14: Therefore you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you. Everyone who profanes it shall surely be put to death; for whoever does any work on it, that soul shall be cut off from the midst of his people.
verses.31:15: For six days work may be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, holy to the LORD. Whoever does work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.
verses.31:16: Therefore the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant.
verses.31:17: Between Me and the children of Israel it is a sign forever; for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.'"
verses.31:18: And He gave to Moses, when He had finished speaking with him upon Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.
verses.32:1: Now when the people saw that Moses delayed in coming down from the mountain, the people assembled around Aaron and said to him, "Arise, make for us gods that shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
verses.32:2: And Aaron said to them, "Take off the rings of gold that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."
verses.32:3: So all the people took off the rings of gold that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
verses.32:4: And he received it from their hand, shaped it with a graving tool, and made it a molten calf. Then they said, "These are your gods, O Israel, that brought you up out of the land of Egypt!"
verses.32:5: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar before it. And Aaron made proclamation and said, "Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD."
verses.32:6: So they rose early on the following day, offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to revel.
verses.32:7: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, "Go, descend, for your people whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt have acted corruptly.
verses.32:8: They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them. They have made for themselves a molten calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, 'These are your gods, O Israel, that brought you up out of the land of Egypt!'
verses.32:10: Now therefore, leave Me alone, that My wrath may burn hot against them and that I may consume them; and I will make of you a great nation."
verses.32:11: Then Moses implored the favor of the LORD his God and said, "Why, O LORD, does Your wrath burn hot against Your people, whom You brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?
verses.32:12: Why should the Egyptians speak, saying, 'With evil intent He brought them out, to slay them in the mountains and to consume them from the face of the earth'? Turn from Your fierce wrath, and relent from this calamity against Your people.
verses.32:13: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself and spoke to them, 'I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land of which I have spoken I will give to your seed, and they shall inherit it forever.'"
verses.32:14: So the LORD relented concerning the calamity that He had spoken of doing to His people.
verses.32:15: Then Moses turned and went down from the mountain, with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hand—tablets written on both their sides; on the one side and on the other they were written.
verses.32:16: Now the tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved upon the tablets.
verses.32:17: When Joshua heard the sound of the people as they shouted, he said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp!"
verses.32:18: But he said, "It is not the sound of the shout of victory, nor the sound of the cry of defeat; it is the sound of singing that I hear."
verses.32:19: And it came to pass, as soon as he drew near to the camp, that he saw the calf and the dancing. Then Moses' wrath burned hot, and he cast the tablets out of his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
verses.32:20: Then he took the calf that they had made, burned it in the fire, and ground it until it was fine powder; and he scattered it upon the face of the water and made the children of Israel drink it.
verses.32:21: And Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you have brought upon them so great a sin?"
verses.32:22: So Aaron said, "Do not let the anger of my lord burn hot; you yourself know the people, that they are set on evil.
verses.32:23: For they said to me, 'Make for us gods that shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
verses.32:24: And I said to them, 'Whoever has any gold, take it off!' So they gave it to me, and I cast it into the fire, and out came this calf."
verses.32:25: Now Moses saw that the people were unrestrained, for Aaron had let them loose to become a derision among their adversaries.
verses.32:26: Then Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Whoever is on the LORD's side, come to me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered together to him.
verses.32:27: And he said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'Let every man fasten his sword upon his side, and go to and fro from gate to gate throughout the camp, and let every man slay his brother, every man his companion, and every man his neighbor.'"
verses.32:28: So the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses, and about three thousand men of the people fell on that day.
verses.32:29: Then Moses said, "Consecrate yourselves today to the LORD, for each man has stood against his son and against his brother, that He may bestow a blessing upon you this day."
verses.32:30: Now it came to pass on the following day that Moses said to the people, "You have sinned a great sin. And now I will go up to the LORD; perhaps I may make atonement for your sin."
verses.32:31: Then Moses returned to the LORD and said, "Alas, this people has sinned a great sin, and has made for themselves gods of gold!
verses.32:32: Yet now, if You will forgive their sin—but if not, I pray, blot me out of Your book that You have written."
verses.32:33: And the LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against Me, him I will blot out of My book.
verses.32:34: Now therefore, go, lead the people to the place of which I have spoken to you. Behold, My angel shall go before you. Nevertheless, in the day of My visitation, I will visit their sin upon them."
verses.32:35: So the LORD struck the people with a plague, because they had made the calf that Aaron made.
verses.33:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, "Depart and go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, 'To your seed I will give it.'
verses.33:2: And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
verses.33:3: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up in your midst, because you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you along the way."
verses.33:4: When the people heard this grievous word, they mourned, and no man put his ornaments upon himself.
verses.33:5: And the LORD said to Moses, "Say to the children of Israel, 'You are a stiff-necked people. If for a single moment I should go up in your midst, I would consume you. Now therefore, take off your ornaments, that I may know what to do with you.'"
verses.33:6: So the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward.
verses.33:7: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far off from the camp, and he called it the Tent of Meeting. And it came to pass that everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the Tent of Meeting that was outside the camp.
verses.33:8: And it came to pass, whenever Moses went out to the tent, that all the people would rise, and each man would stand at the entrance of his tent and gaze after Moses until he entered the tent.
verses.33:9: And it came to pass, when Moses entered the tent, that the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and He would speak with Moses.
verses.33:10: All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would rise and worship, each man at the entrance of his tent.
verses.33:11: Thus the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his attendant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from within the tent.
verses.33:12: Then Moses said to the LORD, "See, You say to me, 'Bring up this people,' yet You have not made known to me whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My sight.'
verses.33:13: Now therefore, if indeed I have found favor in Your sight, make known to me, I pray, Your ways, that I may know You, so that I may find favor in Your sight. And consider that this nation is Your people."
verses.33:14: And He said, "My Presence shall go with you, and I will give you rest."
verses.33:15: Then he said to Him, "If Your Presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here.
verses.33:16: For how then shall it be known that I have found favor in Your sight, I and Your people? Is it not in Your going with us? So shall we be set apart, I and Your people, from every people that is upon the face of the earth."
verses.33:17: And the LORD said to Moses, "This very thing also that you have spoken I will do, for you have found favor in My sight, and I know you by name."
verses.33:18: And he said, "Show me, I pray, Your glory."
verses.33:19: Then He said, "I Myself will cause all My goodness to pass before your face, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you; and I will show grace to whom I will show grace, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy."
verses.33:20: And He said, "You are not able to see My face, for no man may see Me and live."
verses.33:21: And the LORD said, "Behold, there is a place beside Me, and you shall take your stand upon the rock.
verses.33:22: And it shall come to pass, as My glory passes by, that I will place you in the cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
verses.33:23: Then I will remove My hand, and you shall see My back; but My face shall not be seen."
verses.34:1: And the LORD said to Moses, "Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like the first ones, and I will write upon the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you shattered.
verses.34:2: And be prepared for the morning, and ascend in the morning to Mount Sinai, and present yourself to Me there on the summit of the mountain.
verses.34:3: And no man shall go up with you, nor shall any man be seen anywhere on the mountain; neither let the flocks nor the herds graze in front of that mountain."
verses.34:4: So he hewed two tablets of stone like the first ones; and Moses rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, just as the LORD had commanded him, and took in his hand two tablets of stone.
verses.34:5: Then the LORD descended in the cloud and stood with him there, and proclaimed the name of the LORD.
verses.34:6: And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed, "The LORD, the LORD, a God full of compassion and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in lovingkindness and truth,
verses.34:7: preserving lovingkindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, yet by no means acquitting the guilty, visiting the iniquity of fathers upon children and upon children's children, to the third and to the fourth generation."
verses.34:8: And Moses made haste and bowed his head toward the earth and worshiped.
verses.34:9: And he said, "If now I have found favor in Your eyes, O Lord, let the Lord, I pray, go in our midst, for it is a stiff-necked people; and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance."
verses.34:10: And He said, "Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will perform marvels such as have not been created in all the earth, nor among any of the nations; and all the people in whose midst you are shall behold the work of the LORD, for it is an awesome thing that I am doing with you.
verses.34:11: Observe carefully what I command you this day. Behold, I am driving out before you the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.34:12: Take heed to yourself, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are going, lest it become a snare in your midst.
verses.34:13: Rather, you shall tear down their altars, shatter their sacred pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles;
verses.34:14: for you shall not bow down to any other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God,
verses.34:15: lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they play the harlot after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, and someone invites you and you eat of his sacrifice,
verses.34:16: and you take of his daughters for your sons, and his daughters play the harlot after their gods and cause your sons to play the harlot after their gods.
verses.34:17: You shall not make for yourself molten gods.
verses.34:18: You shall keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib; for in the month of Abib you came out from Egypt.
verses.34:19: Everything that opens the womb is Mine, and all your male livestock, the firstborn of ox and sheep.
verses.34:20: But the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. And none shall appear before My presence empty-handed.
verses.34:21: Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; in plowing time and in harvest you shall rest.
verses.34:22: And you shall observe the Feast of Weeks, of the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
verses.34:23: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the Lord, the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.34:24: For I will dispossess nations before you and enlarge your borders; neither shall any man covet your land when you go up to appear before the LORD your God three times in the year.
verses.34:25: You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice together with leaven, nor shall the sacrifice of the Feast of the Passover be left overnight until the morning.
verses.34:26: The choicest of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring to the house of the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
verses.34:27: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words for yourself, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
verses.34:28: So he was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water. And He wrote upon the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
verses.34:29: Now it came to pass, when Moses came down from Mount Sinai, with the two tablets of the Testimony in Moses' hand as he came down from the mountain, that Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had spoken with Him.
verses.34:30: And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to draw near to him.
verses.34:31: Then Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the rulers of the congregation returned to him; and Moses spoke to them.
verses.34:32: And afterward all the children of Israel drew near, and he gave them in commandment all that the LORD had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.
verses.34:33: And when Moses had finished speaking with them, he placed a veil over his face.
verses.34:34: But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out; and he would come out and speak to the children of Israel whatever he was commanded.
verses.34:35: And the children of Israel would see the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses' face shone; and Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with Him.
verses.35:1: Then Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel and said to them, "These are the words which the LORD has commanded you to do:
verses.35:2: Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day there shall be for you a holy day, a Sabbath of solemn rest to the LORD. Whoever does any work on it shall be put to death.
verses.35:3: You shall kindle no fire throughout all your dwellings on the Sabbath day."
verses.35:4: And Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, "This is the word which the LORD commanded, saying,
verses.35:5: 'Take from among you an offering to the LORD. Everyone whose heart is willing, let him bring it as an offering to the LORD: gold, silver, and bronze;
verses.35:6: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, and goats' hair;
verses.35:7: ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
verses.35:9: onyx stones, and stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate.
verses.35:10: And let all who are wise of heart among you come and make all that the LORD has commanded:
verses.35:11: the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;
verses.35:12: the ark and its poles, the mercy seat, and the veil of the screen; the altar of incense and its poles, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the doorway at the entrance of the tabernacle; the hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;
verses.35:13: the table and its poles, all its utensils, and the showbread;
verses.35:14: the lampstand for the light, its utensils, its lamps, and the oil for the light;
verses.35:16: the altar of burnt offering, with its bronze grating, its poles, and all its utensils, and the laver and its base;
verses.35:19: and the finely woven garments for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister as priests.'"
verses.35:20: Then all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.
verses.35:21: And everyone whose heart stirred him, and everyone whose spirit made him willing, came and brought the offering of the LORD for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
verses.35:22: So they came, both men and women, all who were of a willing heart, and brought brooches, earrings, rings, and necklaces, all kinds of articles of gold, every man presenting a wave offering of gold to the LORD.
verses.35:23: And every person with whom was found blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats' hair, ram skins dyed red, or fine leather, brought them.
verses.35:24: Everyone who could contribute an offering of silver or bronze brought it as the offering of the LORD; and everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service brought it.
verses.35:25: And all the women who were wise of heart spun with their hands, and brought what they had spun: the blue, the purple, the scarlet yarn, and the fine linen.
verses.35:26: And all the women whose hearts stirred them with skill spun the goats' hair.
verses.35:27: And the rulers brought the onyx stones, and the stones to be set for the ephod and for the breastplate,
verses.35:28: and the spice and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
verses.35:29: Every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring material for all the work which the LORD had commanded to be done by the hand of Moses, the children of Israel brought as a freewill offering to the LORD.
verses.35:30: And Moses said to the children of Israel, "See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;
verses.35:31: and He has filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of craftsmanship,
verses.35:32: to devise artistic designs, to work in gold, in silver, and in bronze,
verses.35:33: in the cutting of stones for setting, and in the carving of wood, to work in every kind of artistic craftsmanship.
verses.35:34: And He has put it in his heart to teach, both he and Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.
verses.35:35: He has filled them with wisdom of heart to perform every work of an engraver and a designer and an embroiderer, in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and in fine linen, and of a weaver—those who perform every kind of work and who devise artistic designs."
verses.36:1: And Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man in whom the LORD has placed wisdom and understanding to know how to perform all the work of the service of the sanctuary, shall work according to all that the LORD has commanded.
verses.36:2: Then Moses summoned Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, everyone whose heart moved him to come near to the work to perform it.
verses.36:3: And they received from before Moses all the offering that the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to perform it. Still they kept bringing to him freewill offerings morning by morning.
verses.36:4: Then all the skilled men who were performing all the work of the sanctuary came, each man from the work that they were doing.
verses.36:5: And they spoke to Moses, saying, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the service of the work that the LORD has commanded to be done."
verses.36:6: So Moses gave a command, and they sent a proclamation throughout the camp, saying, "Let neither man nor woman prepare any more work for the offering of the sanctuary." Thus the people were restrained from bringing.
verses.36:7: For the material was sufficient for them for all the work to do it, and even to spare.
