verses.36:8: And of the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn they made finely woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, and they made the holy garments for Aaron, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:9: He made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
verses.36:10: And they hammered out thin plates of gold, and he cut them into threads to work into the blue, into the purple, into the scarlet yarn, and into the fine linen, the work of a skilled designer.
verses.36:11: They made shoulder pieces for it, joined together; at its two edges it was joined.
verses.36:12: And the intricately woven band of the ephod that was upon it was of one piece with it and of the same workmanship: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:13: And they fashioned the onyx stones, set in mountings of gold, engraved like the engravings of a signet with the names of the sons of Israel.
verses.36:14: And he placed them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of memorial for the sons of Israel, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:15: He also made the breastplate, the work of a skilled designer, like the workmanship of the ephod: of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen.
verses.36:16: It was square; they made the breastplate doubled over: a span was its length and a span its width when doubled.
verses.36:17: And they set in it four rows of stones: a row of sardius, topaz, and emerald was the first row;
verses.36:18: and the second row: turquoise, sapphire, and diamond;
verses.36:19: and the third row: jacinth, agate, and amethyst;
verses.36:20: and the fourth row: beryl, onyx, and jasper; they were enclosed in gold settings in their mountings.
verses.36:21: And the stones were according to the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, each according to its name, for the twelve tribes.
verses.36:22: And they made upon the breastplate braided chains of corded work, of pure gold.
verses.36:23: They also made two settings of gold and two rings of gold, and they put the two rings on the two edges of the breastplate.
verses.36:24: And they put the two braided cords of gold into the two rings on the edges of the breastplate.
verses.36:25: And the two ends of the two braided cords they fastened to the two settings, and put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod toward its front.
verses.36:26: And they made two rings of gold and placed them on the two edges of the breastplate, on its border that faces inward toward the ephod.
verses.36:27: And they made two rings of gold and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod underneath, toward its front, close by its seam, above the woven band of the ephod.
verses.36:28: And they bound the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue, so that it would rest upon the woven band of the ephod and the breastplate would not come loose from the ephod, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:29: He made the robe of the ephod of woven work, entirely of blue.
verses.36:30: And the opening of the robe was in its midst, like the opening of a coat of mail, with a binding around its opening so that it would not be torn.
verses.36:31: And they made on the hem of the robe pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, finely twisted.
verses.36:32: They also made bells of pure gold, and placed the bells between the pomegranates on the hem of the robe all around, between the pomegranates:
verses.36:33: a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe for ministering, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:34: And they made the tunics of fine linen, of woven work, for Aaron and for his sons,
verses.36:35: and the turban of fine linen, and the ornamental caps of fine linen, and the linen trousers of finely twisted linen,
verses.36:36: and the sash of finely twisted linen, and of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, the work of an embroiderer, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.36:37: And they made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, and inscribed upon it an inscription like the engravings of a signet: "Holiness to the LORD."
verses.36:38: And they fastened a cord of blue to it, to attach it high upon the turban, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.37:1: Then all the wise-hearted men among those performing the work made the tabernacle of ten curtains: of finely twisted linen, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; with cherubim, the work of a skilled designer, he made them.
verses.37:2: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain was four cubits; all the curtains had one measurement.
verses.37:3: And he made the veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen; with the work of a skilled designer he made it with cherubim.
verses.37:4: And he made for it four pillars of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, with their hooks of gold; and he cast for them four sockets of silver.
verses.37:5: He also made a screen for the entrance of the tent, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer;
verses.37:6: and its five pillars with their hooks; and he overlaid their capitals and their bands with gold, and their five sockets were of bronze.
verses.37:7: Then he made the court: for the south side, southward, the hangings of the court were of finely twisted linen, one hundred cubits;
verses.37:8: their pillars were twenty and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.
verses.37:9: And for the north side, one hundred cubits; their pillars were twenty and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.
verses.37:10: And for the west side, hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars were ten and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.
verses.37:11: And for the east side, eastward, fifty cubits.
verses.37:12: The hangings for one side were fifteen cubits; their pillars were three and their sockets three.
verses.37:13: And for the other side—on this side and on that side of the gate of the court—hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars were three and their sockets three.
verses.37:14: All the hangings of the court all around were of finely twisted linen.
verses.37:15: And the sockets for the pillars were of bronze, the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals was of silver; and all the pillars of the court were banded with silver.
verses.37:16: And the screen for the gate of the court was the work of an embroiderer, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely twisted linen; its length was twenty cubits, and its height in breadth was five cubits, corresponding to the hangings of the court.
verses.37:17: And their pillars were four, and their sockets four, of bronze; their hooks were of silver, and the overlaying of their capitals and their bands were of silver.
verses.37:18: And all the pegs for the tabernacle and for the court all around were of bronze.
verses.37:19: These are the inventories of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, which were tallied at the command of Moses, as the service of the Levites, under the hand of Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
verses.37:20: And Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.37:21: And with him was Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, an engraver and skilled designer, and an embroiderer in blue, in purple, in scarlet yarn, and in fine linen.
verses.38:1: Then Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood; two cubits and a half was its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
verses.38:2: He overlaid it with pure gold within and without, and made for it a gold molding all around.
verses.38:3: And he cast for it four rings of gold upon its four feet—two rings on its one side, and two rings on its other side.
verses.38:4: He inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to bear the ark.
verses.38:5: And he made a mercy seat of pure gold; two cubits and a half was its length, and a cubit and a half its breadth.
verses.38:6: He made two cherubim of gold; of hammered work he fashioned them at the two ends of the mercy seat:
verses.38:7: one cherub at the end on the one side, and one cherub at the end on the other side; of one piece with the mercy seat he made the cherubim at its two ends.
verses.38:8: And the cherubim stretched out their wings upward, overshadowing the mercy seat with their wings, with their faces turned toward one another; toward the mercy seat were the faces of the cherubim.
verses.38:9: Then he made the table of acacia wood; two cubits was its length, one cubit its breadth, and a cubit and a half its height.
verses.38:10: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and set the rings upon the four corners that belonged to its four legs. Close beside the frame were the rings, as holders for the poles to bear the table.
verses.38:11: He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. And he made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, to bear the table.
verses.38:12: He also made the vessels that were upon the table—its dishes, its pans, its bowls, and the pitchers with which drink offerings are poured—of pure gold.
verses.38:13: Then he made the lampstand of pure gold; of hammered work he fashioned the lampstand. Its base and its shaft, its cups, its knobs, and its blossoms were of one piece with it.
verses.38:15: And six branches extended from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from its one side, and three branches of the lampstand from its other side.
verses.38:16: Three cups shaped like almond blossoms were on the one branch, with a knob and a blossom, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the other branch, with a knob and a blossom—so for the six branches extending from the lampstand. Their knobs and their branches were of one piece with it; all of it was one hammered piece of pure gold.
verses.38:17: And he made its seven lamps, its wick-trimmers, and its trays of pure gold.
verses.38:18: And he overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings of gold as holders for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
verses.38:22: Then he made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood; five cubits was its length and five cubits its breadth—it was square—and three cubits was its height.
verses.38:23: He made all the utensils of the altar—the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the firepans; all of its utensils he made of bronze.
verses.38:24: And he made for the altar a grate of bronze network under its ledge, reaching from below to its middle. He also cast four rings at the four corners of the bronze grate, as holders for the poles.
verses.38:25: He also made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of sweet spices, the work of a perfumer.
verses.38:26: And he made the laver of bronze and its base of bronze, from the mirrors of the serving women who ministered at the doorway of the tent of meeting.
verses.38:27: From it Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and their feet. Whenever they went into the tent of meeting, and whenever they drew near to the altar, they washed, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.39:1: All the gold that was used for the work in all the labor of the sanctuary—the gold of the wave offering—was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
verses.39:2: And the silver from those who were numbered of the congregation was one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary:
verses.39:3: a beka for each head, half a shekel according to the shekel of the sanctuary, for everyone who passed over to those who were numbered, from twenty years old and above, for six hundred and three thousand, five hundred and fifty men.
verses.39:4: And the hundred talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the sanctuary and the sockets of the veil: one hundred sockets from the hundred talents, one talent for each socket.
verses.39:5: And from the one thousand seven hundred and seventy-five shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals, and joined them with bands.
verses.39:6: And the bronze of the wave offering was seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
verses.39:8: And the sockets of the court all around, and the sockets of the gate of the court, and all the pegs of the tabernacle, and all the pegs of the court all around.
verses.39:9: With it he made the sockets for the doorway of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar, the bronze grate that belonged to it, and all the utensils of the altar.
verses.39:10: Thus all the work of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting was completed. And the children of Israel did according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses; so they did.
verses.39:13: And they brought the tabernacle to Moses—the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;
verses.39:14: the ark of the Testimony with its poles, and the mercy seat;
verses.39:15: the golden altar, the anointing oil, the sweet incense, and the screen for the doorway of the tent;
verses.39:16: the pure lampstand with its lamps, the lamps set in order, all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
verses.39:17: the table, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
verses.39:18: the finely woven garments for ministering in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons to serve as priests;
verses.39:19: the hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, the screen for the gate of the court, its cords and its pegs, and all the utensils for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
verses.39:20: and the covering of ram skins dyed red, and the covering of fine leather, and the veil of the screen.
verses.39:22: According to all that the LORD had commanded Moses, so the children of Israel performed all the work.
verses.39:23: Then Moses looked upon all the work, and behold, they had done it; just as the LORD had commanded, so they had done. And Moses blessed them.
verses.40:1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.40:2: "On the day of the first month, on the first of the month, you shall raise up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
verses.40:3: You shall place there the ark of the Testimony, and you shall screen the ark with the veil.
verses.40:4: And you shall bring in the table and set its arrangement in order, and bring in the lampstand and light its lamps.
verses.40:5: You shall place the altar of gold for incense before the ark of the Testimony, and set the screen for the entrance of the tabernacle.
verses.40:6: Then you shall place the altar of burnt offering before the entrance of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting.
verses.40:8: And you shall set up the court all around, and put up the screen of the gate of the court.
verses.40:9: Then you shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it; you shall consecrate it and all its vessels, and it shall be holy.
verses.40:10: And you shall anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and consecrate the altar; and the altar shall be most holy.
verses.40:12: Then you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and wash them with water.
verses.40:13: And you shall clothe Aaron with the holy garments, and anoint him and consecrate him, that he may minister to Me as priest.
verses.40:14: And you shall bring his sons near and clothe them with tunics.
verses.40:15: You shall anoint them just as you anointed their father, that they may minister to Me as priests; and their anointing shall surely be for them an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations."
verses.40:16: And Moses did so; according to all that the LORD commanded him, so he did.
verses.40:17: And it came to pass in the first month of the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was raised up.
verses.40:18: Moses raised up the tabernacle, laid its sockets, placed its boards, put in its bars, and raised up its pillars.
verses.40:19: He spread out the tent over the tabernacle and placed the covering of the tent above it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.40:20: He took the Testimony and placed it into the ark, set the poles on the ark, and placed the mercy seat on top of the ark.
verses.40:21: Then he brought the ark into the tabernacle, hung the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the Testimony, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.40:22: He placed the table in the tent of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
verses.40:23: And he set the bread in order upon it before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.40:24: He placed the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
verses.40:25: And he lighted the lamps before the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.40:26: He placed the altar of gold in the tent of meeting before the veil.
verses.40:27: And he burned fragrant incense upon it, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.40:29: And he placed the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the grain offering, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
verses.40:33: Then he raised up the court all around the tabernacle and the altar, and put up the screen of the gate of the court. Thus Moses completed the work.
verses.40:34: And the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
verses.40:35: And Moses could not enter the tent of meeting, because the cloud abode upon it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
verses.40:36: And whenever the cloud was lifted up from above the tabernacle, the children of Israel would set out in all their journeys.
verses.40:37: But if the cloud was not lifted up, then they would not set out until the day it was lifted up.
verses.40:38: For the cloud of the LORD was upon the tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.

notes.1:7: The Hebrew verb rendered "teemed abundantly" echoes the creation blessing of Genesis 1:20-21, portraying Israel's growth in Egypt as a fulfillment of God's covenant promise.
notes.1:16: "Birthstool" translates a Hebrew dual noun meaning literally "the two stones," referring to the pair of stones or bricks on which a woman crouched during childbirth.
notes.1:21: "Households" is literally "houses" in Hebrew, indicating that God rewarded the midwives by granting them enduring families and descendants.
notes.2:3: "Ark" renders the same Hebrew word used for Noah's ark in Genesis 6-9, highlighting Moses's rescue through the waters as an act of divine preservation.
notes.2:10: The name Moses resembles the Hebrew verb meaning "to draw out," while also echoing an Egyptian element meaning "child" or "born of."
notes.2:25: The Hebrew ends starkly with "and God knew," expressing God's intimate concern for Israel's plight and His readiness to act.
notes.3:12: "Serve" uses the same Hebrew root as the "bondage" of chapters 1-2, underscoring that Israel is liberated from serving Pharaoh in order to serve God.
notes.3:14: The Hebrew phrase rendered "I AM WHO I AM" uses an imperfect verb that can also mean "I WILL BE WHO I WILL BE," affirming God's eternal, active presence and linking to the covenant name "the LORD" in verse 15.
notes.3:19: Literally "and not by a mighty hand," meaning Pharaoh will stubbornly resist even strong compulsion until God strikes Egypt with His wonders in verse 20.
notes.4:2: The Masoretic Ketiv writes "what is this" as a single contracted word, while the Qere divides it into two words ("what is this"), which is followed in the translation.
notes.4:10: Literally "a man of words" and "heavy of mouth and heavy of tongue," Hebrew idioms expressing a lack of fluency or ease in speaking.
notes.4:18: The Masoretic Hebrew uses the shorter name form Jether in the first clause and the fuller form Jethro in the second clause for Moses' father-in-law.
notes.4:21: The Hebrew verb rendered "harden" literally means to strengthen or make firm, indicating the stiffening of Pharaoh's resolve.
notes.4:25: Zipporah's phrase "bridegroom of blood" is a compressed Hebrew expression connecting her husband's sparing with the blood of her son's circumcision.
notes.5:16: The final clause is terse in Hebrew, literally "and the sin of your people," conveying that the blame for the brick shortfall belongs to Pharaoh's own officials rather than the Israelites.
notes.5:21: Literally "made our odor stink in the eyes of Pharaoh," a vivid Hebrew idiom for rendering someone utterly disfavored and detested.
notes.6:3: "God Almighty" translates Hebrew El Shaddai. The Niphal verb rendered "make Myself known" indicates that the full redemptive significance of the LORD's covenant name had not yet been unveiled to the patriarchs.
notes.6:8: "Lifted up My hand" is a Hebrew idiom for swearing a solemn oath.
notes.6:9: "Brokenness of spirit" is literally "shortness of spirit," expressing deep discouragement and anguish under oppression.
notes.6:12: "Uncircumcised lips" is a Hebrew idiom denoting impeded, hesitant, or unskilled speech, repeated in 6:30.
notes.7:1: Literally "I have made you God to Pharaoh," indicating that Moses would act as God's authoritative representative while Aaron declared his words as his prophet.
notes.7:9: The Hebrew term tannin denotes a large serpent or reptile, distinct from nachash ("serpent") used in 7:15 and 4:3.
notes.7:14: "Stubborn" translates Hebrew kaved (literally "heavy"), one of three verbs describing Pharaoh's hardened heart in this chapter alongside qashah in 7:3 and chazaq in 7:13 and 7:22.
notes.7:19: "Both in wood and in stone" refers to water held in wooden and stone vessels throughout the land of Egypt.
notes.7:26: In the Hebrew Masoretic Text, the announcement of the plague of frogs appears at 7:26-29, corresponding to 8:1-4 in most English versions.
notes.8:2: Hebrew uses the collective singular hatzfardea ("the frog") to depict the overwhelming mass of frogs covering the land.
notes.8:5: Hebrew hitpaer alai, literally "glory over me," is a polite idiom inviting Pharaoh to take the honor of appointing the exact time.
notes.8:11: Hebrew kaved literally means "made heavy" or dull, distinguishing this hardening from chazaq ("grew strong" or stubborn) in 8:15.
notes.8:17: Hebrew arov denotes a dense, mixed swarm of biting insects, traditionally rendered as swarms of flies.
notes.8:19: Hebrew pedut literally means "redemption" or "deliverance," here denoting a separating distinction that spares Israel.
notes.9:12: This is the first time in the plague narratives that the text explicitly states that the LORD Himself hardened Pharaoh's heart.
notes.9:16: Hebrew heemadtikha literally means "I have caused you to stand," conveying that God preserved Pharaoh on the throne to display His power.
notes.9:28: Hebrew qolot Elohim, literally "voices of God," is an idiom for awe-inspiring, mighty thunder.
notes.9:31: Hebrew aviv designates barley that has already formed green ears on the stalk, while givol indicates flax in bud or bloom.
notes.10:1: The Hebrew verb rendered "hardened" literally means "made heavy," conveying a dull or unresponsive heart, whereas verses 20 and 27 employ a different verb meaning "strengthened" or "made resolute."
notes.10:2: The Hebrew verb translated "dealt severely" carries the sense of acting ruthlessly or making a decisive spectacle of judgment against an adversary.
notes.10:10: Pharaoh's remark that "evil is before your faces" preserves the Hebrew ambiguity, which may mean either that Moses and Aaron harbor wicked intent or that calamity awaits them.
notes.10:19: "West wind" is literally "wind of the sea" (the Mediterranean Sea to the west), and "Red Sea" translates the Hebrew designation literally meaning "Sea of Reeds."
notes.11:7: "Move its tongue" renders a vivid Hebrew idiom literally meaning "sharpen its tongue," portraying complete stillness and protection in which not even a dog snarls or barks.
notes.11:8: "Who follow at your feet" translates the Hebrew idiom "who are at your feet," denoting the whole assembly marching under Moses' leadership.
notes.11:10: This summary verse closes the entire cycle of wonders performed before Pharaoh prior to the institution of the Passover and the final plague.
notes.12:3: The Hebrew seh denotes a young animal from the flock, either a sheep or a goat, as clarified in verse 5.
notes.12:6: Literally "between the two evenings," denoting the twilight period between sunset and nightfall.
notes.12:22: The Hebrew saph is rendered "basin" here as the vessel holding the sacrificial blood, though the same term can also mean "threshold."
notes.12:40: The Masoretic Text states directly that the sojourn in Egypt lasted four hundred and thirty years, without the addition of Canaan found in the Samaritan Pentateuch and Septuagint.
notes.12:42: The Hebrew leil shimmurim expresses both the LORD's watchful vigilance in delivering Israel and the people's perpetual night of solemn observance.
notes.13:10: The Hebrew idiom miyyamim yamimah is literally "from days to days," signifying an annual observance from year to year.
notes.13:16: Hebrew totafot denotes frontlets or reminder bands worn between the eyes, paralleling "memorial" in verse nine.
notes.13:18: Hebrew yam-suf is literally "Sea of Reeds," traditionally rendered "Red Sea." Hebrew chamushim means "in battle array" or "in ordered ranks," possibly connected to fivefold military formations.
notes.14:7: Hebrew shalishim refers to elite chariot captains or officers, literally "third-men" serving in the chariot crews.
notes.14:8: Literally "with a high hand," an idiom denoting open boldness and triumphant departure rather than secret flight.
notes.14:20: The Masoretic Hebrew is notably terse, literally "and there was the cloud and the darkness, and it illuminated the night," portraying the pillar bringing darkness toward Egypt while lighting Israel's way.
notes.14:25: The Masoretic text reads wayyasar ("and He took off" or "removed"), indicating that the LORD dislodged the wheels of the Egyptian chariots.
notes.14:31: Literally "the great hand," a Hebrew idiom signifying the mighty power and decisive work of the LORD.
notes.15:2: The Hebrew text here uses Yah, a poetic shortened form of the divine name, rendered "the LORD." The verb rendered "I will extol Him" is a rare poetic form meaning to adorn with praise or to glorify.
notes.15:4: "The Red Sea" renders the Hebrew yam-suph, literally "the Sea of Reeds," following traditional English usage.
notes.15:17: The verse pairs the Tetragrammaton ("the LORD") in the second clause with the title Adonai ("the Lord") in the final clause.
notes.16:2: Ketiv/Qere variant: the written text has a Hiphil verb form, while the traditional reading (Qere), followed here, has a Niphal form; both mean "murmured" or "complained."
notes.16:7: Ketiv/Qere variant: the written text has a Niphal verb form, whereas the traditional reading (Qere), followed here, has a Hiphil form; both carry the sense "you murmur."
notes.16:15: The question "What is it?" renders the Hebrew phrase man hu, providing the wordplay behind the name "manna" (man) in verse thirty-one.
notes.16:36: An omer, one-tenth of an ephah, was a dry measure equivalent to roughly two quarts, or about two liters.
notes.17:3: The Hebrew uses first-person singular suffixes ("me and my children and my livestock"), portraying the complaining congregation as speaking with a single collective voice.
notes.17:7: Massah means "Testing" and Meribah means "Contention" or "Quarreling," commemorating both Israel's dispute with Moses and their testing of the LORD.
notes.17:15: The Hebrew name of the altar is Yahweh-Nissi, literally "The LORD Is My Banner," signifying the LORD as Israel's rallying standard in battle.
notes.17:16: The Hebrew phrase "a hand upon the throne of the LORD" employs a rare shortened form for "throne" and is variously understood as a solemn oath sworn by the divine throne or as Amalek's hostile hand lifted against the LORD's rule.
notes.18:3: The name Gershom plays on the Hebrew word ger ("sojourner" or "resident alien"), recalling Moses' years as an exile in Midian.
notes.18:4: The name Eliezer means "My God Is Help," honoring God's deliverance of Moses from Pharaoh's wrath.
notes.18:11: The final clause is deliberately elliptical in Hebrew, underscoring that the LORD manifested His supremacy over all gods in the very matter by which the Egyptians acted arrogantly against Israel.
notes.18:26: The Masoretic text preserves an unusual archaic imperfect vocalization for "they judged" (yishputu), reflecting customary, ongoing judicial action.
notes.19:5: The Hebrew term segullah ("treasured possession") was used in the ancient Near East for a sovereign's personal, prized treasure distinct from ordinary holdings.
notes.19:13: The Hebrew word translated "trumpet" here (hayyovel) literally designates a ram's horn sounded as a signal, the same term later associated with the Year of Jubilee.
notes.19:19: Hebrew qol ("voice") can mean either articulate speech or thunder, tying God's answer to Moses directly to the awe-inspiring thunderings of verse sixteen.
notes.20:13: In this Hebrew text, verses 13 through 15 order these three commandments as adultery, theft, and murder, matching the sequence found in the Nash Papyrus and Codex Vaticanus of the Septuagint, whereas the standard Masoretic order is murder, adultery, and theft.
notes.20:18: The Hebrew participle literally means seeing, expressing the people's unified sensory perception of both the audible thunder and trumpet and the visible lightning and smoke.
notes.20:25: The Hebrew noun literally denotes a sword or sharp cutting instrument, referring here to an iron chisel used to shape building stones.
notes.21:6: The Hebrew phrase literally reads God; many traditional interpreters understand it as referring to the judges who officiated and rendered legal decisions before God.
notes.21:8: Translates the read form (qere), for himself; the written consonantal form (ketiv) reads not, which would yield who has not designated her.
notes.21:16: In this Hebrew text, the statute against cursing parents stands before the statute against stealing a person in verse 17, matching the sequence in the Septuagint, whereas the standard Masoretic text reverses these two verses.
notes.21:37: Verse numbering follows the Masoretic Hebrew division, in which this verse concludes chapter 21; most English versions number it as Exodus 22:1.
notes.22:1: In Masoretic versification, Exodus 22:1 corresponds to 22:2 in most English Bibles, as the Masoretic Text places the preceding verse at 21:37.
notes.22:7: The Hebrew word elohim here, in 22:8 (where it takes a plural verb), and in 22:27 literally means "God," though traditional interpretation also understands it in judicial contexts as "the judges."
notes.22:28: Literally "your fullness and your tear," poetic expressions for the abundance of the grain harvest and the dripping outflow of wine and olive presses.
notes.23:5: The Hebrew plays on two senses of the verb azav, contrasting refraining from helping with surely assisting to release the fallen animal from its load.
notes.23:17: The Hebrew title ha-Adon YHWH literally reads "the Master, the LORD," a solemn designation often rendered "the Lord GOD" in traditional English versions.
notes.23:28: The Hebrew collective singular ha-tsirah ("the hornet") is understood either literally as swarms of stinging insects or figuratively as overwhelming terror sent by God.
notes.23:31: "The River" denotes the Euphrates, the traditional northeastern boundary, and "the Red Sea" is literally "the Sea of Reeds" (Yam Suph).
notes.24:8: Hebrew karat literally means "cut," reflecting the ancient Near Eastern idiom of "cutting a covenant" ratified by sacrificial blood.
notes.24:10: Hebrew livnat hassappir denotes a paved work or tiled surface of blue sapphire stone, likely lapis lazuli in ancient usage.
notes.24:11: Hebrew atzilei is a rare term meaning "nobles" or "chief men," and the verb chazah ("beheld") distinguishes solemn or visionary sight from ra'ah ("saw") in verse ten.
notes.25:5: The exact identity of Hebrew techashim is uncertain; scholars variously understand it as fine tanned leather or the hides of marine animals such as dugongs or dolphins.
notes.25:17: Hebrew kapporet derives from a root associated with covering and atonement, traditionally rendered "mercy seat" as the golden lid over the ark of the Testimony.
notes.25:30: Hebrew lechem panim literally means "bread of the face" or "bread of the Presence" (traditionally "showbread"), echoing "before Me" (literally "before My face") in the same clause.
notes.25:31: Hebrew kaftor denotes the rounded ornamental bulb or calyx positioned beneath each almond blossom along the lampstand's central shaft and branches.
notes.25:39: A biblical talent (Hebrew kikkar) was a large standard of weight equal to roughly seventy-five pounds.
notes.26:3: The phrase "one to another" renders a feminine Hebrew idiom literally meaning "a woman to her sister," used throughout this chapter for paired curtains, loops, and tenons.
notes.26:14: "Fine leather" translates a Hebrew phrase whose precise meaning is uncertain, variously understood as fine tanned hides, sea-cow or dugong skins, or traditionally badger skins.
notes.26:24: "Completely joined" follows the Masoretic reading meaning "complete" or "whole," complementing the opening term meaning "coupled" or "twinned" to describe the reinforcement of the two rear corners.
notes.26:31: The Hebrew distinguishes the "skillful designer" (vv. 1, 31), who wove cherubim into the inner tabernacle curtains and the veil, from the "embroiderer" (v. 36; 27:16), who fashioned the outer screens.
notes.27:8: "As it was shown to you" renders an active Hebrew verb used impersonally (literally "as He showed you"), and the closing plural "so shall they make it" points to the skilled workers who will construct the altar.
notes.27:18: "Fifty cubits throughout" translates a Hebrew idiom literally reading "fifty by fifty," signifying a uniform width of fifty cubits at both ends of the court.
notes.27:21: "Tent of meeting" appears here for the first time in Exodus, designating the sanctuary as the appointed place where the LORD meets with Israel.
notes.28:17: The exact modern mineralogical identifications of several gemstones in the breastpiece remain uncertain; traditional English equivalents are used here.
notes.28:29: In this Hebrew critical text, verse 29 directly follows verse 22 and combines the fastening of the braided gold cords to the breastpiece and ephod with Aaron bearing the names of the sons of Israel before the LORD.
notes.28:30: Urim and Thummim literally mean Lights and Perfections, sacred objects placed within the breastpiece of judgment by which the high priest sought divine guidance.
notes.28:41: The Hebrew idiom rendered ordain them literally reads fill their hand, signifying formal installation into priestly service.
notes.29:9: Hebrew literally reads "fill the hand of Aaron and the hand of his sons," the standard priestly idiom for ordination and installation into office (used also in vv. 29, 33, and 35).
notes.29:13: The Hebrew verb here denotes turning a sacrifice into ascending smoke upon the altar, distinguishing sacred offering from ordinary burning with fire outside the camp in v. 14.
notes.29:39: "At twilight" translates the Hebrew idiom literally meaning "between the two evenings," designating late afternoon toward dusk (also in v. 41).
notes.29:40: "A tenth of an ephah" translates the Hebrew dry measure issaron, roughly two quarts; a hin was a liquid measure of about one gallon, making a fourth of a hin roughly one quart.
notes.30:8: "At twilight" translates the Hebrew idiom meaning "between the two evenings," referring to the period between sunset and full dusk.
notes.30:12: "Take the census" translates a Hebrew idiom literally meaning "lift up the head," and "for his life" renders the Hebrew word denoting both life and soul.
notes.30:24: A hin was a Hebrew liquid measure of approximately one gallon, or nearly four liters.
notes.30:34: Stacte, onycha, and galbanum were rare aromatic resins and spice ingredients compounded in equal portions with pure frankincense for sacred use alone.
notes.31:10: "Finely woven garments" renders a Hebrew phrase referring either to intricately braided priestly vestments or to the woven cloths used to cover the sanctuary furnishings in transit.
notes.31:13: "It is a sign" translates the feminine pronoun referring to the Sabbath, written here and in verses 14 and 17 with the standard Pentateuchal spelling read as the feminine form.
notes.31:17: "Was refreshed" translates a Hebrew verb linked to the root for breath or soul, an anthropomorphic expression for God's restful delight upon the completion of creation.
notes.32:4: The Hebrew noun rendered "graving tool" denotes a chisel or stylus used to shape metal, though some interpreters understand the related root as binding the gold in a pouch or mold.
notes.32:14: The Hebrew verb translated "relented" expresses the LORD's compassionate turning back from executing a threatened judgment in response to Moses' intercession.
notes.32:18: Moses' reply employs a wordplay between the Qal infinitive meaning "shouting" (in victory or defeat) and the Piel infinitive of the same root meaning "singing" or "chanting."
notes.32:29: Literally "Fill your hand today to the LORD," the customary Hebrew idiom for priestly consecration and ordination.
notes.32:32: Moses' plea breaks off mid-sentence in a solemn Hebrew ellipsis ("if You will forgive their sin—") before stating his willingness to be blotted out.
notes.33:6: The phrase "from Mount Horeb" indicates that the Israelites laid aside their ornaments beginning at Horeb and continuing onward as a mark of contrition.
notes.33:14: Literally "My face shall go," using "face" as the idiomatic expression for God's personal, manifest Presence accompanying His people.
notes.33:19: The repeated verbal clauses ("I will show grace to whom I will show grace") employ a Hebrew idiom declaring the sovereign freedom of God's favor and mercy.
notes.34:6: Hebrew chesed denotes steadfast covenant love and mercy, while emet conveys both truth and enduring faithfulness.
notes.34:7: The clause translated "by no means acquitting the guilty" renders an emphatic Hebrew infinitive absolute construction underscoring the certainty of divine justice.
notes.34:28: Grammatically, the subject of "wrote" could be Moses continuing the preceding verbs, or the LORD fulfilling His promise in verse one (compare Deuteronomy ten, verse four).
notes.34:29: The Hebrew verb qaran is cognate with the noun for "horn" and here signifies rays of radiant light shining from the skin of Moses' face.
notes.35:7: The precise meaning of the Hebrew term techashim is uncertain; traditionally rendered "badger skins," it likely refers to fine leather or sea-cow hides.
notes.35:12: In this critical Hebrew text, the furnishings of the ark, the incense altar with the anointing oil and entrance screen, and the hangings of the court are grouped together within this verse.
notes.35:31: Hebrew ruach Elohim ("the Spirit of God") signifies the divine Spirit empowering Bezalel with practical wisdom, understanding, and artistic mastery for the sanctuary work.
notes.36:1: Literally "wise of heart," the Hebrew idiom denotes both practical craftsmanship and God-given artistic discernment.
notes.36:8: In the Saints Hebrew Critical Text, the making of the priestly garments follows directly after the freewill offerings (corresponding to Exodus 39:1-31 in the traditional Masoretic order). The phrase "finely woven garments" renders Hebrew bigdei serad, referring to braided or specially worked liturgical cloths.
notes.36:11: The translation follows the Qere (read form) reading the plural suffix "its two edges," whereas the Ketiv (written form) preserves an older singular-like orthography.
notes.36:17: The exact ancient mineralogical identifications of several gemstones in the breastplate remain debated; traditional English equivalents are used here for the twelve stones.
notes.37:1: The Hebrew shifts from plural ("made") to singular ("he made them"), reflecting Bezalel's master supervision over the artisans. In this critical text, the curtains, veil, entrance screen, and court are grouped together in chapter 37.
notes.37:6: Hebrew rashim (literally "heads") refers to the tops or capitals of the pillars, and chashuqim to their decorative bands or connecting rods.
notes.37:19: Hebrew pequdei denotes the official accounting or inventory of the tabernacle's materials, compiled under the supervision of Ithamar.
notes.38:7: Ketiv reads qetsoto (an orthographic spelling lacking the plural yod), while Qere reads qetsotav ("its ends"), which is followed here as "its two ends."
notes.38:11: This verse preserves a textual doublet recording both the making of gold-overlaid acacia poles and the making of the poles specifically to bear the table.
notes.38:26: The "serving women" (hatsobe'ot) were women who performed organized service at the entrance of the tent of meeting; their polished metal mirrors supplied bronze for the laver.
notes.39:3: A beka was an ancient weight equal to half a sanctuary shekel, approximately five to six grams of silver.
notes.39:8: The arrangement of verses 8 and 9 follows this edition's order of the bronze inventory, placing the court sockets and pegs before the governing verb in verse 9.
notes.39:17: "Bread of the Presence" (lehem hapanim) is traditionally known as showbread, the twelve loaves set continually upon the golden table before the LORD.
notes.39:20: The Hebrew term rendered "fine leather" (tehashim) is of uncertain identification, variously understood as fine tanned leather, dyed goatskins, or the hides of marine animals such as dugongs.
notes.40:2: The Hebrew reads literally 'on the day of the first month, on the first of the month,' marking the opening day of the new year for the inauguration of the sanctuary.
notes.40:4: The phrase 'set its arrangement in order' reflects the cognate Hebrew expression for arranging the bread of the Presence and its appointed vessels upon the table.
notes.40:15: The Hebrew doubles the verb 'to be' to emphasize the enduring certainty of the Aaronic priesthood conferred by their anointing.
notes.40:35: The verb rendered 'abode' shares the same Hebrew root as 'tabernacle,' underscoring that the sanctuary was now inhabited by the abiding presence of the LORD.
